SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.claim: Al Imran’s account of changing events uses active verbs; al-Anam instead foregrounds God's attributes and power with nominal and participial forms, then uses a verb for the living’s movement. Each form suits its context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/r1.anchor: فالسياق كله حركة وتغيير وتبديل فجاء بالصغية الفعلية الدالة على التحدد والتغيير والحركة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r7.claim: They include an alif in وجعل الليل سكنا; Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai omit it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r7.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر / وجعل اليل سكنا / بألف

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r1.claim: Al-Samin directs this phrase to his earlier discussion of فالق الحب.

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r2.claim: The majority read الإصباح with initial hamza kasra, treating it as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r2.anchor: والجمهور على كسر الهمزة وهو المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r3.speaker: الليث والزجاج والفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r3.claim: Al-Layth, al-Zajjaj, and al-Farra say الصبح والصباح والإصباح all mean the beginning of the day.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r3.anchor: وقال الليث والزجاج: إن الصبح والصباح والإصباح واحد

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r4.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Talha transmits from Ibn Abbas that الإصباح is sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r4.anchor: وقيل: الإصباح ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل، رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r5.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r5.claim: Mujahid is reported to interpret الإصباح as the illumination of dawn.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو إضاءة الفجر، نقل ذلك عن مجاهد

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r6.claim: Al-Samin prefers the original verbal-noun sense, later used as a name for morning, as الإمساء names evening.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الإصباح في الأصل مصدر سمي به الصبح وكذا الإمساء

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r7.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line contrasts morning with the long night and supplies poetic usage of الإصباح.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r7.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: 2005 ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجل

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء وعيسى بن عمر
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r8.claim: These readers open the hamza in الأصباح, treating it as a plural of صبح like قفل/أقفال and برد/أبراد.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وعيسى بن عمر: الأصباح: بفتح الهمزة وهو جمع صبح

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r9.claim: The cited poem uses الأمساء and الأصباح as plurals of مسي and صبح with fatḥa; with kasra, they are verbal nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r9.anchor: أفنى رياحا وبني رياح تناسخ الأمساء والأصباح

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r10.claim: A reading puts الإصباح in the accusative by deleting tanwin where two sukuns meet.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r10.anchor: وقرئ/ " فالق الإصباح " بنصب الإصباح وذلك على حذف التنوين لالتقاء الساكنين

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r11.claim: The cited poetic fragment ولا ذاكر الله إلا قليلا illustrates deletion of tanwin at a meeting of sukuns.

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r12.claim: The accusative forms والمقيمي الصلاة and لذآئقو العذاب exemplify carrying the nun as tanwin.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r12.anchor: و { لذآئقو العذاب } [الصافات: 38] بالنصب حملا للنون على التنوين

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r13.speaker: سيبويه والمبرد
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r13.claim: Sibawayh permits deleting tanwin at a meeting of sukuns only in poetry; al-Mubarrad permits it in ordinary usage.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r13.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه لا يجيز حذف التنوين لالتقاء الساكنين إلا في شعر، وقد أجازه المبرد في السعة

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r14.speaker: يحيى والنخعي وأبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r14.claim: Yahya, al-Nakhaʿi, and Abu Haywa read فلق as a past-tense verb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r14.anchor: وقرأ يحيى والنخعي وأبو حيوة: " فلق " فعلا ماضيا

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r15.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r15.claim: Abd Allah likewise read the earlier فالق الحب as the past verb فلق.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r15.anchor: أن عبد الله قرأ الأولى كذلك

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r16.claim: Al-Samin argues the contrasting readings show that recitation is a transmitted, followed Sunnah.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r16.anchor: وهذا أدل دليل على أن القراءة عندهم سنة متبعة

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r17.claim: Zamakhshari answers the question about فلق الصبح by positing an omitted noun: فالق ظلمة الإصباح.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r17.anchor: قلت: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يراد: فالق ظلمة الإصباح، يعني أنه على حذف مضاف

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r18.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r18.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r18.claim: Zamakhshari’s other analysis takes الإصباح as the dawn pillar split from the day’s whiteness and brightness.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r18.anchor: والثاني: أن يراد فالق الإصباح الذي هو عمود الفجر عن بياض النهار وإسفاره

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r19.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r19.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r19.claim: Al-Samin notes Arabic descriptions of dawn as breaking open and calling dawn فلق, meaning something split.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r19.anchor: وقالوا: انشق عمود الفجر وانصدع، وسموا الفجر فلقا بمعنى مفلوق

SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r20.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r20.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96/r20.claim: The anonymous line تفري ليل عن بياض نهار illustrates night splitting away from daylight.

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r1.claim: The continuation cites al-Taʾi: the blue of dawn appears before its white light.

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r2.claim: A reading puts both فالق and جاعل in the accusative as words of praise.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r2.anchor: وقرئ: فالق وجاعل بالنصب على المدح

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r3.claim: A further anonymous poem describes the dawn column splitting away, illustrating the image of dawn breaking open.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r3.anchor: وأنشد غيره: 2010 فانشق عنها عمود الفجر جافلة

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r4.speaker: الكوفيون والباقون
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r4.claim: The Kufans read جعل as a past verb, while others read جاعل; the outline allows both, with الليل accusative for Kufans and genitive for the others.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r4.anchor: قوله: { وجاعل الليل } قرأ الكوفيون: " جعل " فعلا ماضيا، والباقون بصيغة اسم الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r5.claim: The Kufan past-tense reading suits the following past verbs, including جعل لكم النجوم and أنشأكم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r5.anchor: ووجه قراءتهم له فعلا مناسبته ما بعده فإن بعده أفعالا ماضية نحو

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r6.claim: On the Kufan reading, سكنا is either a second object if جعل means ‘make,’ or a prospective circumstantial accusative if it means ‘create.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r6.anchor: ويكون " سكنا ": إما مفعولا ثانيا على أن الجعل بمعنى التصيير، وإما حالا

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r7.claim: For the other reading, جاعل can mean past, which al-Samin considers apparent and supported by the Kufan reading.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r7.anchor: وأما قراءة غيرهم فجاعل يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى المضي، وهو الظاهر، ويؤيده قراءة الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r8.speaker: البصريون والكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r8.claim: For a past active participle, Basrans generally require أل for governance, though views differ; al-Kisaʾi allows it to govern without restriction.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r8.anchor: والماضي عند البصريين لا يعمل إلا مع أل خلافا لبعضهم في منع إعمال المعرف بها، وللكسائي في إعماله مطلقا

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r9.claim: If جاعل is past, Basrans make سكنا accusative under an omitted verb, whereas al-Kisaʾi lets the participle govern it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r9.anchor: ف " سكنا " منصوب بفعل مضمر عند البصريين، وعلى مقتضى مذهب الكسائي ينصبه به.

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد السيرافي
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r10.claim: Al-Sirafi says a participle taking two objects may govern its second in the past when annexation to the first prevents annexation to the second.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r10.anchor: وقد زعم أبو سعيد السيرافي أن اسم الفاعل المتعدي إلى اثنين يجوز أن يعمل في الثاني وإن كان ماضيا

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r11.claim: Another rationale is that annexation makes the participle resemble a form defined by أل, so it governs freely.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r11.anchor: لأنه بالإضافة أشبه المعرف بأل فعمل مطلقا

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r12.claim: If جاعل denotes present or future, it directly governs سكنا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r12.anchor: وأما إذا قلنا إنه بمعنى الحال والاستقبال فنصبه به

SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r13.claim: سكن is a passive-form noun meaning ‘made still,’ like القبض meaning ‘that which is seized.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:97/r13.anchor: و " سكن " فعل بمعنى مفعول كالقبض بمعنى مقبوض

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r1.claim: The majority read الشمس and القمر accusatively; under the Kufan past reading, they coordinate with the objects of جعل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { والشمس والقمر حسبانا } الجمهور بنصب " الشمس " و " القمر "

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r2.claim: حسبانا has the same two parses as سكنا: a second object or a circumstantial accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r2.anchor: و " حسبانا " فيه الوجهان في " سكنا " من المفعول الثاني والحال

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r3.claim: If the participle denotes past, the accusatives require an elided verb: وجعل الشمس.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r3.anchor: فلا بد من إضمار فعل ينصبهما أي: وجعل الشمس

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r4.claim: Even on a nonpast participle parse, Sibawayh makes the accusatives depend on an omitted verb, not the genitive complement’s syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r4.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه أيضا أن النصب بإضمار فعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r5.claim: Sibawayh illustrates the omitted-verb parse with هذا ضارب زيد الآن أو غدا أو عمرا, where عمرا is accusative under an understood verb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r5.anchor: تقول: " هذا ضارب زيد الآن أو غدا أو عمرا " بنصب عمرو، وبفعل مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r6.speaker: غير سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r6.claim: Other grammarians allow the accusatives to coordinate with the syntactic position of the genitive governed by جاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r6.anchor: وعلى رأي غيره يكون النصب على محل المجرور

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r7.claim: The line هل أنت باعث دينار لحاجتنا أو عبد رب uses accusative عبد and is compatible with either account.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r7.anchor: هل أنت باعث دينار لحاجتنا أو عبد رب أخاعون بن مخراق

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r8.claim: Zamakhshari proposes coordinating الشمس والقمر with the position of الليل, since the participle denotes continuous action rather than a time-specific past event.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " أو يعطفان على محل " الليل ". فإن قلت: كيف يكون ل " الليل " محل

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r9.claim: The Shaykh rejects this rationale: an unbounded participle cannot govern, and its genitive complement has no syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r9.anchor: وهذا ليس بصحيح، إذا كان لا يتقيد بزمن خاص، وإنما هو للاستمرار، فلا يجوز له أن يعمل

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r10.claim: The Shaykh cites ألقيت كاسبهم في قعر مظلمة for an unbounded participle; a time-specific past without أل cannot govern for Basrans, unlike marked past, present, or future.

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r11.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r11.claim: Even if the continuous participle governs, Sibawayh forbids coordination with the position of its genitive complement; an omitted verb is needed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#2/r11.anchor: وعلى تقدير تسليم أن الذي للاستمرار يعمل فلا يجوز العطف على محل مجروره

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r1.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r1.claim: Abu Haywa reads الشمس والقمر in the genitive, coordinating by form.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: { والشمس والقمر } جرا نسقا على اللفظ

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r2.claim: A noncanonical reading puts الشمس والقمر in the nominative as a topic, requiring an omitted predicate such as مجعولان حسبانا or مخلوقان حسبانا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r2.anchor: وقرئ شاذا { والشمس والقمر } رفعا على الابتداء، وكان من حقه أن يقرأ " حسبان " رفعا على الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r3.claim: Al-Samin answers that on the accusative parse حسبانا is a second object or circumstantial state that describes the sun and moon, so the same predication issue applies.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r3.anchor: والحال لا بد وأن تكون صادقة على ذي الحال

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد والأخفش وأبو الهيثم والمبرد
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r4.claim: These authorities take حسبان as a plural of حساب, like ركاب/ركبان and شهاب/شهبان.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r4.anchor: أنه جمع، فقيل: جمع حساب كركاب وركبان وشهاب وشهبان

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls it a plural of حسبانة, but al-Samin rejects this because حسبانة means a piece of fire, not intended here.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " هو جمع حسبانة " وهو غلط؛ لأن الحسبانة القطعة من النار

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r6.speaker: ابن السكيت
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit analyzes حسبان as a verbal noun like رجحان and نقصان, while حساب is a noun rather than a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r6.anchor: بل هو مصدر كالرجحان والنقصان والخسران، وأما الحساب فهو اسم لا مصدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r7.claim: Zamakhshari distinguishes ḥusbān as the verbal noun of حساب and ḥisbān as the verbal noun of حسبت, paralleling الكفران والشكران.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r7.anchor: والحسبان بالضم مصدر حسبت يعني بالفتح كما أن الحسبان بالكسر يعني مصدر حسبت بالكسر

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r8.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r8.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya treats حسبان and حساب as verbal nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: بل الحسبان والحساب مصدران وهو قول أحمد بن يحيى

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد عن أبي زيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r9.claim: Abu ʿUbayd, citing Abu Zayd, quotes على الله حسباني as poetic evidence for حسبان as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r9.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيد عن أبي زيد في مجيء الحسبان مصدرا قوله: 2013

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r10.claim: Al-Samin recalls Zamakhshari’s analysis of ملك يوم الدين and says the absence of a specific time makes its annexation pure and definite, not a governing active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#3/r10.anchor: قلت: وقد ذكر الزمخشري في أول الفاتحة في

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r1.claim: حسبانا is accusative either as an object or a circumstantial accusative, as with سكنا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r1.anchor: وانتصاب " حسبانا " على ما تقدم من المفعولية أو الحالية

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r2.speaker: ثعلب عن الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r2.claim: Thaʿlab transmits al-Akhfash’s parse with an omitted preposition: the sun and moon move بحسبان, like لمن خلقت طينا meaning من طين.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r2.anchor: وقال ثعلب عن الأخفش: إنه منصوب على إسقاط الخافض والتقدير: يجريان بحسبان

SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r3.claim: ذلك may point to the preceding splitting, the making, or all reports from فالق الحب through حسبانا.
SAMIN-DURR:6:96#4/r3.anchor: وقوله: " ذلك " إشارة إلى ما تقدم من الفلق أو الجعل أو جميع ما تقدم

ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r2.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ and al-ṣubḥ mean the same; fāliq may mean creator or splitter of dawn, the latter returning to creator.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r2.anchor: معنى الإصباح والصبح وأحد، جائز أن يكون خالق الإصباح وجائز أن يكون معناه شاق الصبح، وهو راجع إلى معنى خالق الصبع.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r3.claim: Accusative al-shamsa wa-l-qamara is the reading; genitive is possible as objects of jāʿil, since the participle carries the meaning of jaʿala.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r3.anchor: النصب في الشمس والقمر هي القراءة. والجر جائز على معنى وجاعل (الشمس والقمر حسبانا)، لأن في جاعل معنى جعل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r4.claim: With a past action, an active participle normally annexes its object; most grammarians and Kufa grammarians agree, though some Kufans allow accusative, as in muʿṭī Zaydan dirhaman.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r4.anchor: لأن أسماء الفاعلين إذا كان الفعل قد رفع أضيفت إلى ما بعدها لا غير تقول هذا ضارب زيد أمس. فإجماع النحويين أنه لا يجوز في زيد النصب، وعلى ذلك أكثر الكوفيين، وبعض الكوفيين يجيز النصب.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r5.claim: Sakanan is accusative through the sense of jaʿala; in a two-object construction like muʿṭī, the second accusative is carried by the corresponding past verb.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273#2/r5.anchor: فإذا قلت هذا معطي زيد درهما فنصب الدرهم محمول على أعطى.

ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n81/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n81/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n81/r1.claim: The sun and moon follow a definite reckoning.
ASAD-NOTES:6:95#n81/r1.anchor: Lit., "to be [according to] a definite reckoning".

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r3.claim: The same contrast appears in 6:96: dawn, associated with motion and life, has the noun فالق, while tranquil night is described with the verb جعل.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p643/r3.anchor: فالليل فيه السكون والهدوء فجاءت معه الصيغة الفعلية (جعل الليل سكناً)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.claim: Tafṣīl originates in separating things; it can mean broad explanation or the presentation of several distinct matters.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.anchor: التفصيل هو إما أن يكون التبيين والفصل هو الحجز بين الشيئين وهذا الأصل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.claim: The passage moves across separate subjects—seeds, dawn, sun and moon, then stars—so its many different signs are appropriately called tafṣīl.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.anchor: إنتقل من الحب والنوى إلى الإصباح ثم الشمس والقمر ثم النجوم، مواضيع أخرى ثم ينتقل يذكر أموراً كثيرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.claim: The conjunction wāw gives general coordination and may join one sentence to another; it does not itself express a causal relation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.anchor: الواو لمطلق الجمع، الجمع المطلق، قد يكون عطف جملة على جملة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.claim: Fa commonly marks cause and consequence, as in درس فنجح; when the first action leads to the next, fa is used rather than wāw.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.anchor: الفاء تفيد السبب، هذا المشهور في معناها (درس فنجح)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r3.claim: When fa is causal with an imperative or prohibition, the following imperfect verb is subjunctive, as in لا تأكل كثيراً فتمرض.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r3.anchor: سواء كانت عاطفة "لا تأكل كثيراً فتمرض" يُنصب بعدها المضارع

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: The discussion moves from God's feats in the earth, seen in seeds and stones, to His splendor in the sky.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: people should also observe His splendour in the sky above them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Dawn splitting darkness parallels God's splitting a fruit-stone to bring forth a tree.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: Just as He creates a tree by splitting a fruit-stone, He also brings forth the dawn after slicing through the veil of darkness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Night provides comfort and rest, relieving the fatigue of the day so people can become fresh again.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: He has created the night to provide comfort and rest and alleviate people from tiredness of the day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: The night-rest/day-work sequence is similarly described in al-Nabaʾ 78:9–11.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: In verses 9-11 of S ūrah al-Nabā, it is similarly stated

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: Night prepares people to begin their chores again by day and work for their livelihood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: God sends the day after the night that people can start again with their chores and work for their livelihood.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: The ordered alternation of dawn, evening, night, and day shows that they all come and go at God's command, not under different creators.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: all of them come and go at the behest of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: After night and day, the passage turns to the two great signs appearing in them, the sun and moon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: After the night and the day, the two great signs that appear in them are referred to: the sun and the moon.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.claim: The sun and moon precisely follow their laws and calendars, mark days, months, and years, and produce the seasons.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p84/.anchor: There is a law and calendar for each of them which they minutely obey and observe and not the slightest deviate from them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: Though in the sky, the sun and moon diligently serve earth's inhabitants without seeking praise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The phrase draws the inference from the sun and moon's vigilance, like the call of a heart reflecting logically on the universe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: depict the inference that can be drawn from the vigilance shown by the sun and the moon.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The sun and moon have no share in divinity; they are machinery placed and tasked by a powerful, knowledgeable God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: They are like parts of a machinery fitted in their place by the powerful and knowledgeable God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The universe's harmony, including its opposites, testifies that one powerful, knowledgeable God governs it all.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: there exists amazing harmony between its opposite elements.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The universe is purposeful rather than amusement, and a Day of Judgement must come to manifest the Creator's wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: the universe has been created with a purpose which is bound to materialize.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The ordered cosmos implies that humans should live by the Creator's directives, harmonizing their lives with the universe; this is the path to success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: the Creator of human beings wants them too lead a life according to his directives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: Islahi says the Qur'an also adduces prophethood from this cosmic testimony, a point he develops under 55:5.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: There the Qur’ān has also adduced prophethood from this testimony.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: means “planning.” The attribute al-‘Az īz signifies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: Al-ʿAzīz denotes immense power and dominance; al-ʿAlīm denotes unfathomable knowledge encompassing wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: The attribute al-‘Az īz signifies His immense power and dominance and the attribute al-‘Al īm signifies His unfathomable knowledge

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: God is beyond the universe's system, and His power, knowledge, and wisdom embrace everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: God is not part of this system of the universe. He is above and beyond everyone.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r1.claim: These readers use جاعل with an alif; al-Fārisī prefers it because it parallels the preceding active participle فالق, maintaining noun with noun, as in several Qur’anic and poetic constructions.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: وجاعل الليل سكنا بألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r2.claim: These readers use جعل without an alif: the preceding participle فالق refers to the past and functions like a past verb, so a verb can follow it; the coordinated sun and moon are likewise accusative as with a past verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p361/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: وجعل الليل سكنا بغير ألف

QIRAAT-ER:6:96:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:4#1/r1.claim: The active participle jāʿilu replaces perfect jaʿala, paralleling fāliqu so both predicates in Beat A are participles.
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: active participle jāʿilu instead of perfect verb jaʿala — parallels fāliqu in Beat A

QIRAAT-ER:6:96:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:5#1/r1.claim: With jāʿilu, layl changes from the accusative object of jaʿala to a genitive iḍāfa construction, restructuring the syntax.
QIRAAT-ER:6:96:5#1/r1.anchor: In the jāʿilu variant, layl shifts from accusative (object of jaʿala) to genitive (iḍāfa with jāʿilu)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فالق الإصباح ﴾ قال الصبح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r2.claim: Qatada says the sun and moon move according to a calculation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ والشمس والقمر حسبانا ﴾ قال يدوران بحساب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r1.claim: الإصباح is a verbal noun used as a name for morning, as illustrated by a poet's address to the long night to give way to morning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r1.anchor: مصدر سمي به الصبح، قال الشاعر: ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r2.claim: Though darkness seems to split open at dawn, the phrase can elide مضاف and mean splitting dawn's darkness, or mean splitting it away from daylight's whiteness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r2.anchor: أن يكون ذلك على حذف مضاف أي فالق ظلمة الإصباح وهي الغبش الذي يلي الصبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r3.claim: Arabic also calls dawn's emergence a crack or split; فلق can name the dawn as something split open, a passive sense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r4.claim: Another explanation is that فالق means bringing morning into view: the cause, splitting, is named for its effect, manifestation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r4.anchor: أو يكون المعنى مظهر الإصباح إلا أنه لما كان الفلق مقتضيا لذلك الإظهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r5.claim: A further gloss takes فالق الإصباح to mean creator of morning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses الإصباح as the light of dawn.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report of Ibn Abi Talha, explains it as sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r7.anchor: وروى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أن الإصباح ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r8.speaker: الليث والفراء والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r8.claim: Al-Layth, al-Farra, and al-Zajjaj define الصبح, الصباح, and الإصباح as the start of the day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r8.anchor: وقال الليث والفراء والزجاج: الصبح والصباح والإصباح أول النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r9.claim: A poet pairs مساء and صباح to mean evening and morning; another transmission explains the forms as plurals of مسى and صبح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r9.anchor: قال: أفنى رياحا وبني رياح ... تناسخ الإمساء والإصباح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains the phrase as creator of day and night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: معناه خالق النهار والليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r11.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r11.claim: Al-Kirmani says God cleaves the column of dawn out of darkness and uncovers it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r11.anchor: وقال الكرماني: شاق عمود الصبح عن الظلمة وكاشفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r12.speaker: الحسن وعيسى وأبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r12.claim: Al-Hasan, Isa, and Abu Rajaʾ read الإصباح with fatḥa on its hamza as the plural of صبح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى وأبو رجاء الأصباح بفتح الهمزة جمع صبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r13.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r13.claim: One group reads الإصباح in the accusative while dropping the tanwin of فالق; Sibawayh permits this only poetically at two adjacent quiescent letters, while al-Mubarrad allows it in prose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r13.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بنصب الإصباح وحذف تنوين فالق وسيبويه إنما يجوز هذا في الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r14.speaker: النخعي وابن وثاب وأبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r14.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Ibn Waththab, and Abu Haywa read فلق الإصباح as a past-tense verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r14.anchor: وقرأ النخعي وابن وثاب وأبو حيوة فلق الإصباح فعلا ماضيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r15.claim: After signs in earthly plants and animals, the passage adduces celestial conditions; dawn's cleaving is more striking because celestial phenomena impress people more.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r15.anchor: لما استدل على باهر حكمته وقدرته بدلالة أحوال النبات والحيوان وذلك من الأحوال الأرضية استدل أيضا على ذلك بالأحوال الفلكية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r16.claim: Sakan is passive in sense: something people seek company in and find reassuring; night lets people rest after the work of day, and fire is similarly called the comforting one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r16.anchor: والسكن فعل بمعنى مفعول أي مسكون إليه وهو من تستأنس به وتطمئن إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r17.claim: The stated wisdom of night as repose is linked to the verse saying God made night so people may rest in it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r18.speaker: الأخفش ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r18.claim: Al-Akhfash parses حسبانا as the plural of حساب, like شهاب/شهبان; Yaʿqub instead takes it as a verbal noun, with حساب as the ordinary noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r18.anchor: والحسبان جمع حساب كشهاب وشهبان قاله الأخفش أو مصدر حسب الشيء والحساب الاسم قاله يعقوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas says حسبانا refers to the counting of days, months, and years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r19.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني بها عدد الأيام والشهور والسنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r20.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r20.claim: Qatadah glosses حسبانا as light or brightness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r21.claim: It is also said that fire is called حسبانا; the following segment cites Mujahid's hadith gloss comparing the term to a mill axle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p592/r21.anchor: قيل: وتسمى النار حسبانا وفي صحيح البخاري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r1.speaker: تاج القراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r1.claim: Taj al-Qurraʾ reads حسبانا as حساب: sun and moon travel by measured course, letting people count days, months, and years; the sun's cycle is 365¼ days and the moon's 28.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r1.anchor: قال تاج القراء: حسبانا أي بحساب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r2.claim: Another explanation is that sun and moon run by a counted measure until they reach the end of their appointed terms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r2.anchor: وقيل: يجريان بحساب وعدد لبلوغ نهاية آجالهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says their revolutions and courses provide a calculation by which people know the times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جعلهما على حساب لأن حساب الأوقات يعلم بدورهما وسيرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r4.claim: The Kufans read جعل as a past-tense verb; because فالق has a past sense, جعل coordinates naturally with it, and sun and moon are accusatives coordinated with الليل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وجعل الليل فعلا ماضيا لما كان فالق بمعنى المضي حسن عطف وجعل عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r5.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r5.claim: The other seven readers have وجاعل, an active participle annexed to الليل; Abu Ali says Basrans treat it as past and supply an implied verb for سكنا, while al-Sirafi allows the past participle to govern it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r5.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة وجاعل باسم الفاعل مضافا إلى الليل والظاهر أنه اسم فاعل ماض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r6.speaker: الكسائي وهشام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r6.claim: Al-Kisai and Hisham allow a past active participle to govern; on their analysis سكنا is its direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r6.anchor: وأما من أجاز إعمال اسم الفاعل الماضي وهو الكسائي وهشام فسكنا منصوب به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r7.speaker: يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r7.claim: Yaʿqub reads ساكنا; al-Dani says this attribution is not sound.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r8.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r8.claim: Abu Haywa reads الشمس والقمر in the genitive, coordinating them with الليل سكنا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة بجر والشمس والقمر حسبانا عطفا على الليل سكنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r9.claim: For the accusative reading with وجاعل, al-Zamakhshari offers coordination with الليل's syntactic position as one analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أو يعطفان على محل الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r10.claim: On the majority accusative reading, with جاعل الليل, the sun and moon can be accusatives governed by an implied جعل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r10.anchor: فعلى قراءة جاعل الليل ينتصبان على إضمار فعل أي وجعل الشمس والقمر حسبانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r11.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's continuing-participle argument for giving الليل a syntactic position: a participle without a specific time cannot govern or leave its complement a stable slot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p593/r11.anchor: وملخصه أنه ليس اسم فاعل ماضيا فلا يلزم أن يكون عاملا فيكون للمضاف إليه موضع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r1.claim: For Basrans, an active participle governs in the past only with أل, or when present or future; an unmarked past participle does not govern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r1.anchor: فإما أن يكون ماضيا دون أل فلا يعمل إذ ذاك عند البصريين أو بأل أو حالا أو مستقبلا فيجوز إعماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r2.claim: Sibawayh's rule is that a participle's complement cannot be coordinated by position when that position is not fixed; a time-specific active participle can govern its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r2.anchor: مذهب سيبويه، فلو قلت: زيد ضارب عمرو الآن أو غدا أو خالدا لم يجز أن تعطف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r3.claim: The cited line with كاسب not bound to a particular time illustrates why a continuing, non-time-specific participle does not govern by the Basran rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r3.anchor: ألقيت كاسبهم في قعر مظلمة فليس الكاسب هنا مقيدا بزمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r4.claim: ذلك may refer to this making, the cleaving and making together, or all the preceding reports beginning with the splitting of grain and kernel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r4.anchor: أي ذلك الجعل أو ذلك الفلق والجعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r5.claim: Al-Aziz is the One who overpowers and subdues all these things; al-Alim knows every such state and nothing else escapes His knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r5.anchor: تقدير العزيز الغالب الذي كل شيء من هذه في تسخيره وقهره العليم الذي لا يعزب عنه شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r6.claim: Attributing all this to divine measure shows God alone acts by choice; natural necessity or inherent properties are not its cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p594/r6.anchor: وفي جعل ذلك كله بتقديره دلالة على أنه هو المختص الفاعل المختار لا أن ذلك فيها بالطبع ولا بالخاصية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r1.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ is either the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning He is the splitter of dawn, or another predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r1.anchor: خبر لمبتدأ محذوف أي هو فالق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r2.claim: With kasra, iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun used as a name for dawn; the cited Imruʾ al-Qays line witnesses this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r2.anchor: بكسر الهمزة مصدر سمي به الصبح

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads iṣbāḥ with fatḥ as a plural of ṣubḥ, like qufl and aqfāl; the cited verse uses al-amsāʾ and al-aṣbāḥ as plurals, while kasra and fatḥ can each be verbal nouns and plurals.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بالفتح على أنه جمع صبح كقفل وأقفال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain fāliq as Creator, while several others say it means splitter.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r4.anchor: والفالق الخالق على ما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r5.claim: The apparent difficulty that darkness, rather than dawn, seems to split is answered by distinguishing true dawn, spread horizontally, from false dawn, a vertical streak brighter at its top and followed by darkness; dawn may be split from daylight or the implied darkness of dawn from the night.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r5.anchor: واستشكل بأن الظاهر أن الظلمة هي التي تفلق عن الصبح وأجيب بأن الصبح صبحان صادق وهو المنتشر ضوؤه معترضا بالأفق وكاذب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r6.claim: On the true-dawn reading, God splits it from daylight, or the implied phrase is splitting dawn's darkness with dawn; the dark horizon is pictured as a sea cleaved by a channel of light.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r6.anchor: أي فالق ظلمة الاصباح بالاصباح وذلك لأن الأفق من الجانب الغربي والجنوبي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r7.claim: On the false-dawn reading, God splits it from the darkness of late night; the true and false forms of dawn are evident to observation.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r7.anchor: وعلى الثاني فايراد أنه سبحانه فالقه عن ظلمة آخر الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r8.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r8.claim: Astronomers explain dawn and twilight as illumination in the vaporous atmosphere when the sun approaches the eastern horizon and recedes from the western one.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r8.anchor: إلا أن في سبب ذلك كلاما لأهل الهيئة حاصله أن الصبح وكذا الشفق استنارة في كرة البخار لتقارب الشمس من أفق المشرق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r9.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r9.claim: Their account describes the vapor sphere as heated, rising earth and water particles surrounding Earth, about fifty-one miles high, spherical and denser near Earth, with density varying but not obscuring what lies beyond.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r9.anchor: وقد تحقق أن كرة البخار عبارة عن هواء متكاثف بما فيه من الأجزاء الأرضية والمائية المتصاعدة من كرتيهما بتسخين الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r10.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r10.claim: They describe Earth's broad shadow as a cone dividing the sunlit half of Earth from the dark half, with light and darkness making one daily circuit as opposed markers.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r10.anchor: وان للارض ظلا على هيئة مخروط قاعدته دائرة عليها تكاد تكون عظيمة وهي مواجهة للشمس ورأسه في مقابلها وتنقسم الأرض بهذه القاعدة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r11.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r11.claim: Sunlight surrounds the Earth's shadow and reaches the celestial spheres; it passes through the faint parts of the Moon and Mercury spheres without reflection, while clear air does not accept light and denser vapor does.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r11.anchor: وأن شعاع الشمس محيط بمخروط الظل من جميع جوانبه ومنبث في جميع الافلاك سوى مقدار يسير من فلك القمر وفلك عطارد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r12.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r12.claim: In this account day is the time the Earth's shadow cone lies below the horizon, and night the time it lies above it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p227#2/r12.anchor: وان النهار مدة كون ذلك المخروط تحت الافق والليل مدة كونه فوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r1.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r1.claim: As the sun nears the eastern horizon, its shadow cone inclines west; the cone's surrounding light first appears at the point nearest the observer as an elevated vertical streak, while the lower horizon looks dark because it is farther away and the air is dense: this is false dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r1.anchor: إذا ازداد قرب الشمس من شرقي الافق ازداد ميل المخروط إلى غريبة ولا يزال كذلك حتى يرى الشعاع المحيط به وأول ما يرى هو الاقرب إلى موضع الناظر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r2.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r2.claim: When the sun approaches the eastern horizon further, light spreads horizontally and grows, erasing the first streak like stars or lamps erased by sunlight; this is true dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r2.anchor: ثم إذا قربت من الافق الشرقي رؤي الضوء معترضا منبسطا يزداد لحظة فلحظة وينمحي الأول بهذا الضياء القوي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r3.speaker: التذكرة وشرح سيد المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r3.claim: A geometrical explanation imagines a plane through the Sun, Earth, shadow-cone axis, and base center, forming an acute triangle whose base is the horizon; as the cone's apex moves west, its eastern angle narrows and its western angle widens.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r3.anchor: وتوضيح ما ذكر على ما في التذكرة وشرح سيد المحققين أنه يتوهم لبيان ذلك سطح يمر بمركز الشمس والأرض وبسهم المخروط ومركز قاعدته فيحدث مثلث حاد الزوايا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r4.speaker: التذكرة وشرح سيد المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r4.claim: The geometric account argues that the closest visible point on the eastern side lies inside the triangle, nearer the observer than the side's horizon intersection; although the whole dense side is illuminated, the nearest point is seen most truly, explaining the two dawns.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p228/r4.anchor: فوجب أن يقع داخل المثلث فيما بين طرفي الضلع الشرقي وقد تبين أن موضعه أقرب إلى الناظر من موضع اتصاله بالأفق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r1.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r1.claim: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī denies that false dawn comes from the solar disk: light should already spread broadly through the eastern atmosphere and grow continuously, so a narrow vertical streak must be created directly by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r1.anchor: والامام الرازي أنكر كون الصبح الكاذب من أثر قرص الشمس وإنما هو بتخليق الله تعالى ابتداء قال لأن مركز الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r2.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī's argument also implies that true dawn is directly created by God: the sun below the horizon cannot face any part of Earth's surface, and light only falls on a body facing its source.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r2.anchor: ويفهم من كلامه أيضا أن الصبح الثاني كالصبح الأول ليس الا بتخليق الفاعل المختار ويمتنع أن يكون من تأثير قرص الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r3.claim: An anticipated counterargument says the sun below Earth could illuminate the air beneath it, which would successively illuminate adjoining air above ground until the light reaches us.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p229/r3.anchor: فان قالوا : لم يجوز أن يقال الشمس حين كونها تحت الأرض توجب إضاءة ذلك الهواء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r1.claim: Alusi rejects Ibn al-Haytham’s account that air receives and reflects sunlight: transparent, colorless air cannot take light as a quality.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r1.anchor: وعلى هذا عول أب علي بن الهيثم في المناظر فالجواب : أن هذا باطل من وجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r2.claim: Dense vapor or smoke cannot explain dawn: more such material at the horizon should make dawn brighter, yet the observed relation is opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r2.anchor: لو كان كذلك لكان كلما كانت الأبخرة والأدخنة في الأفق أكثر وجب أن يكون ضوء الصباح أقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r3.claim: The horizon argument also fails: if air took sunlight as a quality, the eastern air here should brighten after midnight when the sun is above the opposite peoples.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r3.anchor: وحيث لم يكن كذلك علمنا أن الهواء لا يقبل كيفية النور في ذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r4.speaker: أحمد بن حجر الهيثمي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar says astronomers’ lengthy account of false dawn rests on conjecture and a philosophers’ premise, and explains neither its brighter upper part nor its disappearance before darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r4.anchor: وذكر أفضل المتأخرين العلامة أحمد بن حجر الهيثمي أن لأهل الهيئة في تحقيق الصبح الكاذب كلاما طويلا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r5.claim: Those who assign false dawn an hour likely mean a variable stretch of time, since it lengthens and shortens; the claim may concern estimation rather than sight.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r5.anchor: وقدروها بساعة والظاهر أن مرادهم مطلق الزمن لأنها تطول تارة وتقصر أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r6.speaker: بعض أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r6.claim: Some astronomers deny that false dawn disappears, saying it merely diminishes until it merges into true dawn; Alusi suggests this may be true by calculation but not observation.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r6.anchor: وزعم بعض أهل الهيئة عدم انعدامه وإنما يتناقص حتى ينغمر في الصادق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r7.speaker: مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r7.claim: A report in Muslim warns not to be misled by Bilal’s call or the vertical streak of dawn until that streak spreads across the horizon.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r7.anchor: وفي خبر مسلم لا يعرنكم أذان بلال ولا هذا العارض لعمود الصبح حتى يستطير

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r8.claim: Alusi reads ʿāriḍ as a light appearing on the dawn ray and the reference to breathing as its delayed release; the first burst is broader than what follows, matching observation.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r8.anchor: ويؤخذ من تسميته عارضا للثاني شيئان أحدهما أنه يعرض للشعاع الناشيء عنه الصبح

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r9.claim: False dawn is an incidental signal whose purpose is to wake sleepers near the intended true dawn, helping them attain the merit of praying early.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r9.anchor: ثانيهما أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أشار بالعارض إلى أن المقصود بالذات هو الصادق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r10.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r10.claim: A report cited from Ahmad distinguishes the elongated white false dawn from the red, horizontal true dawn, supporting Alusi’s account.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r10.anchor: وفي حديث عند أحمد ليس الفجر الأبيض المستطيل في الأفق ولكن الفجر الأحمر المعترض

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r11.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the sun has three hundred openings and rises each day through one; Alusi uses it to support his opening-and-release explanation of dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن للشمس ثلثمائة كوة تطلع كل يوم من كوة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r12.speaker: القرافي والأصبحي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r12.claim: Al-Qarafi, al-Asbahi, and others explain the apparent vanishing: whiteness rises before dawn and disappears from most eyes, though a keen observer can still see it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p230/r12.anchor: وللقرافي المالكي وغيره كالاصبحي من الشافعية فيه كلام يوضحه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r1.speaker: ابن بشير المالكي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r1.claim: Ibn Bashir says false dawn is sunlight as the sun nears the horizon; once eyes adapt to it, observers think it has vanished although it remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r1.anchor: وذكر ابن بشير المالكي أنه من نور الشمس إدا قربت من الافق فإذا ظهرت أنست به الابصار

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r2.speaker: الأصبحي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r2.claim: Al-Asbahi transmits a view held by many Shafiʿis that false dawn disappears after appearing and later returns to the same place at night.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r2.anchor: ونقل الأصبحي أن بعضهم ذكر أنه يذهب بعد طلوعه ويعود مكانه ليلا وهو كثير من الشافعية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر البصري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r3.claim: Abu Jaʿfar describes false dawn about two hours before daybreak as a vertical pillar reaching a quarter of the sky, thin above and broad below; visibility varies by season and weather.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r3.anchor: وأن أبا جعفر البصري بعد أن عرفه بأنه عند بقاء نحو ساعتين يطلع مستطيلا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r4.claim: The claim that false dawn’s upper end is brighter does not conflict with descriptions of it as narrow above: the former applies at first appearance, the latter nearer true dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r4.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا ما تقدم من أن أعلاه أضوأ لأن ذلك عند أول الطلوع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r5.speaker: راصد غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r5.claim: An observer who watched for about fifty years says false dawn never vanished; it descends to meet true dawn in the dark and they become one dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r5.anchor: رده بانه رصده نحو خمسين سنة فلم يره غاب وإنما ينحدر ليلتقي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r6.speaker: بعض المؤقتين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r6.claim: Some timekeepers identify false dawn with the Milky Way when dawn occurs in the Saʿd stations; Alusi notes this would limit it to roughly two months yearly.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r6.anchor: وبعض المؤقتين يقول : هو المجرة إذا كان الفجر بالسعود ويلزمه أن لا يوجد إلا نحو شهرين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r7.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r7.claim: Some say false dawn is a ray emerging from a layer in Mount Qaf; al-Qarafi rejects this because he says the mountain does not exist.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r7.anchor: قال القرافي : وقال آخرون هو شعاع يخرج من طباق بجبل قاف

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r8.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas describe an ocean beyond our land, then Mount Qaf, then further lands, seas, and mountains repeated seven times; Alusi says the Companion’s unseen report has marfuʿ status.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r8.anchor: ما جاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من طرق خرجها الحفاظ

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r9.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allah ibn Burayda describes Qaf as an emerald mountain encircling the world beneath the sky; a similar account is attributed to Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r9.anchor: وأخرج بعض اولئك عن عبد الله بن بريدة أنه جبل من ذمرد محيط بالدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r10.claim: Mujahid is also reported to describe Mount Qaf as an emerald mountain encircling the world beneath the sky.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r11.claim: Alusi rejects al-Qarafi’s categorical claim that Qaf lacks evidence: reports are evidence if that means any indication, and probabilistic evidence suffices for this matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r11.anchor: كما اندفع بذلك قوله : لا وجود له اندفع قوله أثره : ولا يجوز اعتقاد ما لا دليل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r12.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r12.claim: Astronomers say false dawn continually appears and fades; Alusi finds their technical account obscure and prefers variation with seasons, viewing conditions, and atmospheric qualities to explain its seeming disappearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r12.anchor: ثم نقل عن القرافي عن أهل الهيئة أنه يظهر ثم يخفيدائما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r13.claim: Alusi ranks direct divine creation of dawn light as more plausible than a ray from Qaf, and that ray as more plausible than the sun itself emerging through a Qaf opening.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r13.anchor: أن القول بحدوث ضوء الصبح بمجرد خلق الله تعالى لا عن سبب عادي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r14.speaker: غياث الدين جمشيد الكاشي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r14.claim: The comparison invokes estimates that the sun is about 166 Earths in volume, or 326 according to Ghiyath al-Din Kashani, making its passage through a mountain opening implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p231/r14.anchor: أو ثلاثمائة وستة وعشرون مثلا لها على ما قاله غياث الدين جمشيد الكاشي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r1.claim: Even if the Qaf report is authentic and marfuʿ in status, Alusi says it should be interpreted; repeated journeys around Earth found no enclosing mountain, and the seven-sea, seven-mountain cosmography is doubtful. Omnipotence does not establish occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r1.anchor: والخبر في ذلك إن صح وقلنا : إن له حكم المرفوع مما ينبغي تأويله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r2.claim: Alusi says many people’s inclination on the cause of dawn favors the astronomers’ account.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r2.anchor: والذي تميل إليه قلوب كثير من الناس في أمر الصبح ما ذكره أهل الهيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r3.speaker: أرسطوخس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r3.claim: Aristarchus proves geometrically that when a sphere receives light from a larger sphere, more than half of it is illuminated.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r3.anchor: وقد بين أرسطوخس في الشكل الثاني من كتابه في جرم النيرين أن الكرة إذا اقتبست الضوء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r4.speaker: أرسطوخس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r4.claim: Aristarchus also shows that two unequal spheres can be enclosed by a cone whose vertex faces the smaller sphere and which touches each along a circle.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r4.anchor: وقد بين أيضا في الشكل الأول من ذلك الكتاب أن كل كرتين مختلفتين أمكن أن يحيط بهما مخروط

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r5.speaker: أهل الهيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r5.claim: In the astronomical account, the Earth and Sun define a cone whose small tangent circle divides the lit and dark portions of Earth; vaporous air outside Earth’s shadow remains sunlit but is unseen at night because it is distant.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r5.anchor: وقد حققوا أن المستنير من الهواء كرة البخارسوى ما دخل في ظل مخروط الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r6.claim: As the shadow cone stays opposite the Sun, its axis points along the noon circle at midnight, then shifts westward; the sunlit vaporous air becomes visible as eastern whiteness before dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r6.anchor: ففي منتصف الليل يكون على دائرة نصف النهار وبعد ذلك يميل إلى جانب الغروب لحظة فلحظة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r7.claim: This geometry blocks the Imam’s objection: the opposite peoples’ daylight after midnight does not entail that our eastern quarter is illuminated, because their relative positions differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا لا يلزم في الصورة التي ذكرها الإمام من مجاوزة مركز الشمس دائرة نصف الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r8.claim: Alusi accepts the spheres and cone described by astronomers, but says believing a claim known to contradict a necessary religious truth or certain proof is unbelief or error.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r8.anchor: والتزام القول بالكروية والمخروط ونحو ذلك مما ذكره أهل الهيئة لا بأس به

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r9.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232/r9.claim: An unnamed reading has fāliq in the accusative as an expression of praise.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r1.speaker: النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r1.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi reads al-aṣbaḥ in place of al-iṣbāḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ النخعي ( فالق الاصبح ) ( وجعل الليل سكنا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r2.claim: Night is a place of rest and ease for those tired by day; anything a person finds repose and companionship in can be called sakan, including a spouse, beloved, or fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r2.anchor: أي يسكن إليه من يتعب بالنهار ويستأنس به لاسترواحه فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r3.claim: Qatada, in a report from Ibn Abi Hatim, interprets night as the time in which every bird and animal settles.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة أن المعنى يسكن فيه كل طير ودابة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r4.claim: Similar interpretations are reported from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: night is inhabited, in the sense of quiet and settledness.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r4.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن عابس ومجاهد رضي الله تعالى عنهم فالمراد حينئذ جعل الليل مسكونا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r5.claim: The sense of night as a time of settling is linked to the wording of 10:67, “that you may rest in it.”
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r5.anchor: أخذا له من السكون أي الهدوء والاستقرار كما في قوله تعالى : ( تسكنوا فيه )

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r6.speaker: سائر السبعة إلا الكوفيين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r6.claim: All of the seven readers except the Kūfans read jāʿil in the nominative; an anomalous reading has it accusative, while al-layl is genitive by annexation in both.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ سائر السبعة إلا الكوفيين ( جاعل ) بالرفع وقريء شاذا بالنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r7.speaker: كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r7.claim: Many grammarians take sakanan as governed by an implied verb, since the active participle here denotes the past and ordinarily cannot govern its object.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r7.anchor: ونصب ( سكنا ) عند كثير بفعل دل عليه هذا الوصف لا به لأنه يشترط

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي وبعض الكوفيين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and some Kūfan grammarians allow an active participle to govern in the past, analogizing it to the verb whose meaning it contains.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r8.anchor: وجوز الكسائي وبعض الكوفيين عمله بمعنى الماضي مطلقا حملا له على الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r9.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r9.claim: Some grammarians allow past governance when the active participle bears the definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r9.anchor: وبعضهم جوز عمله كذلك إذا دخلت علي أل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r10.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r10.claim: Others allow the participle to govern its second object when it is annexed to its first, because this resembles an article-bearing form.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r10.anchor: وآخرون جوزوا عمله في الثاني إذا أضيف إلى الأول لشبهه بالمعرف باللام

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r11.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r11.claim: Another analysis lets the participle govern because the intended making is continuous across different times, not confined to the past.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r11.anchor: واختار بعضهم كونه الناصب أيضا لكن باعتبار أن المراد به الجعل المستمر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r12.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r12.claim: The learned grammarians distinguish this from a true adjective of established quality, whose continuous sense requires that such usage be well known and common.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r12.anchor: ولا يجري على هذا مجرى الصفة المشبهة لأن ذلك كما قال المحققين فيما قصد به الاستمرار

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r13.claim: On the reading under discussion, sakanan is the second object of jaʿala.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r13.anchor: ونصبه في قراءتنا على أنه مفعول ثان لجعل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r14.claim: A further option takes jaʿala to mean “produce,” transitive to one object, with sakanan accusative as a circumstantial expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r14.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ( جعل ) بمعنى أحدث المتعدي لواحد فيكون نصبا على الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r15.claim: The Sun and Moon can coordinate with al-layl; when al-layl is genitive, they may instead be governed by the implied verb for sakanan or a similar verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r15.anchor: معطوفان على ( الليل ) وعلى قراءة من جره يكون نصبها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r16.claim: Another analysis coordinates Sun and Moon with the grammatical position of al-layl, since its annexation to the participle is not a true genitive relation on the past-tense analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r16.anchor: وقيل : العطف على محل ( الليل ) المجرور فان اضافة الوصف اليه غير حقيقية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r17.speaker: قراءة غير مسماة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r17.claim: The Sun and Moon are also read in the genitive, and in the nominative with an omitted predicate meaning that they are made subject to reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r17.anchor: وقريء بالجر وهو ظاهر وبالرفع على الابتداء والخبر محذوف أي مجعولان حسبانا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r18.claim: The Sun and Moon move through varying cycles by which people calculate times for worship and transactions; alternatively, they themselves are calculated.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r18.anchor: أي على أدوار مختلفة يحسب فيها الأوقات التي نيط بها العبادات والمعاملات

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r19.speaker: أبو الهيثم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r19.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes ḥusbānan as a collective plural of ḥisāb, like rukbān from rikāb; Alusi considers that unlikely here.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r19.anchor: وعن أبي الهيثم أن ( حسبانا ) جمع حساب مثل ركبان وركاب وشهبان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r20.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r20.claim: The majority take “that” to refer especially to the preceding arrangement of night, Sun, and Moon; its demonstrative distance signals the arrangement’s elevated rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r20.anchor: والجمهور على الأول وهو الظاهر وما فيه من معنى البعد للإيذان بعلو منزلة المشار إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r21.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r21.claim: Al-Ṭabarsī takes “that” to point to all the preceding phenomena: dawn’s splitting, night as repose, and the Sun and Moon as measures.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r21.anchor: وقال الطبرسي : إلى ما تقدم من فلق الاصباح وجعل الليل سكنا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r22.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means the overpowering One whom nothing can resist, including the specified motions of the Sun and Moon.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p232#2/r22.anchor: الغالب القاهر الذي لا يتعاصاه شيء من الأشياء التي من جملتها تسييرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233/r1.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is exhaustive in knowledge of every thing, including the worldly and otherworldly benefits contained in the celestial motions.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233/r1.anchor: المبالغ في العلم بجميع المعلومات التي من جملتها ما في ذلك التسيير من المصالح المعاشية والمعادية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.claim: God splits the column of dawn from night's darkness and makes it clear, initiating and illuminating the morning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r1.anchor: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وكاشفه [وهو أول ما يبدو من النهار يريد مبدئ الصبح وموضحه]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains it as the creator of daytime.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: خالق النهار، والإصباح مصدر كالإقبال والإدبار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.claim: Al-isbah is a verbal noun like iqbal and idbar, meaning illumination, and here denotes dawn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r3.anchor: والإصباح مصدر كالإقبال والإدبار، وهو الإضاءة وأراد به الصبح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r4.claim: Night is made a time in which God's creatures rest.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.speaker: أهل الكوفة وإبراهيم النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.claim: The Kufans read jaʿala as a past verb with al-layl in the accusative; Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi reads the phrase with faliq al-isbah and jaʿala al-layl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة: " وجعل " على الماضي، " الليل " نصب اتباعا للمصحف، وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي {فالق الإصباح}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.claim: The sun and moon follow a known reckoning and do not exceed it before reaching the ends of their courses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r6.anchor: جعل الشمس والقمر بحساب معلوم لا يجاوزانه حتى ينتهيا إلى أقصى منازلهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.claim: Hisaban is a verbal noun like al-hisab.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r7.anchor: والحسبان مصدر كالحساب، {ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم}

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r1.claim: The phrase can mean splitting the dawn's column from night-darkness or from daylight's whiteness, or splitting the darkness of early dawn, the dimness just before morning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r1.anchor: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل أو عن بياض النهار، أو شاق ظلمة الإصباح

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r2.claim: Iṣbāḥ is originally the verbal noun of aṣbaḥa, 'to enter morning,' and is used for dawn itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r2.anchor: والإصباح في الأصل مصدر أصبح إذا دخل في الصباح سمي به الصبح

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r3.claim: The hamza is also read with fatḥa as a plural; another reading puts al-iṣbāḥ in the accusative as a praise expression.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r4.claim: Night is rest because the day's fatigue settles through repose, or because creatures dwell in it; the latter sense is linked to 27:86.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r4.anchor: يسكن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته فيه من سكن إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r5.claim: The accusative may depend on an implied verb, as jaʿil has past-tense force, supported by the Kūfan reading wa-jaʿala al-layl and by fāliq meaning falaqa; alternatively it may depend on jaʿil if the making is continuously renewed across times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r5.anchor: ونصبه بفعل دل عليه جاعل لا به

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r6.speaker: قراءة الكوفيين
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r6.claim: The Kūfan readers recite the verb in the past tense, wa-jaʿala al-layl, construing it with the preceding phrase.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r6.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة الكوفيين { وجعل اليل } حملا على معنى المعطوف عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r7.claim: Sun and moon may coordinate with the syntactic position of al-layl, supported by their genitive reading; the author prefers taking them as accusatives governed by an implied jaʿala.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r7.anchor: ويشهد له قراءتهما بالجر والأحسن نصبهما بجعل مقدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r8.claim: The sun and moon are also read in the nominative, with an omitted predicate meaning 'made' or 'appointed.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r8.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر محذوف أي مجعولان

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r9.claim: They move in differing calculated cycles by which times are reckoned and serve as instruments of reckoning; ḥusbān is either a verbal noun of ḥasaba or a plural of ḥisāb like shihāb/shuhbān.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r9.anchor: على أدوار مختلفة يحسب بهما الأوقات ويكونان علمي الحسبان

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r10.claim: That points to making the sun and moon instruments for reckoning time.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r11.claim: The Almighty has subdued the sun and moon and set them moving in their particular courses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r11.anchor: الذي قهرهما وسيرهما على الوجه المخصوص

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r12.claim: God knows how the two luminaries are managed and which of their possible cycles is most beneficial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:96/r12.anchor: بتدبيرهما والأنفع من التداوير الممكنة لهما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r9.claim: The passage moves from the lower, familiar world to the celestial realm; its signs of renewed life also answer Abraham’s argument against deifying light, darkness, and stars.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r9.anchor: شارحا لما أشار إليه الخليل عليه السلام في محاجة قومه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r10.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means bringing dawn into being by splitting night’s darkness; common usage attributes the split to dawn without ambiguity.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r10.anchor: وحقيقته : فالق ظلمة الليل عن الصباح , لكنه لما كثر استعماله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r11.claim: Falaq can also mean disclosure: the cause, splitting, expresses its result, bringing what was hidden into view.
