BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r11.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد بالفلق الكشف , لأنه يكشف من المفلوق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r12.claim: The form al-iṣbāḥ evokes entering the morning, allowing the phrase to mean splitting stillness with light or with the movement that follows dawn.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r12.anchor: وعبر عن الصباح بهذه الصيغة التي يقال المدخول في الصبح لتصلح لإرادة فلق السكون بالنور أو غيره عن التصرف بالحركة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r13.claim: God makes the dark night a repose in which and toward which people settle and rest.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r13.anchor: بما يكون من إظلامه { سكنا } يسكن الناس فيه وإليه ويستريحون فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p678/r14.claim: The author identifies the verse as an example of ihtibāk, a paired ellipsis structure.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r1.claim: The phrasing omits motion in the first expression but indicates it through repose, while the second omits spreading and indicates it through the splitting of dawn.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r1.anchor: حذف من الأول الحركة ودل عليها بالسكن , وحذف من الثاني السدل ودل عليه بالفلق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r2.claim: Dawn includes false and true dawn; the false dawn is stronger evidence: it first appears as a white thread, darkens, then true dawn spreads, showing light is created and darkness persists by God's decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r2.anchor: لأن الإصباح يشمل الفجر الكاذب والصادق , والأول أقوى دلالة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r3.claim: He attaches the sun and moon to the grammatical position of night; making means ongoing ordering through all times, not simply illumination that would make the annexation literal.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r3.anchor: عاطفا على محل { والليل } لأن جاعلا ليس بمعنى المضيء فقط لتكون الإضافة حقيقية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r4.claim: The sun produces both daybreak and night, through rising and setting, while the moon is a sign of night; their courses organize worldly needs through the four seasons, ripening fruits and bringing harvests.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r4.anchor: { والشمس } أي التي ينشأ عنها كل منهما , هذا عن غروبها وهذا عن شروقها { والقمر } أي الذي هوآية الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r5.claim: The sun and moon are measures and markers by which reckoning is known through their revolutions and courses.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r5.anchor: ذوي حسبان وعلمين عليه , لأن الحساب يعلم بدورهما وسيرهما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r6.claim: The intensive verbal noun signals the great, pervasive benefit of celestial reckoning, including religious duties; worshippers have no part in their other benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r6.anchor: المصدر المبني على هذه الصيغة البليغة إشارة إلى أن الحساب بهما أمر عظيم كبير النفع كثير الدخول

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r7.claim: The ordering is God's invincible decree: He compels the sun and moon along their courses and governs human affairs; His knowledge sets an unchanging, balanced measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r7.anchor: أي التقدير العظيم الذي تقدم من الفلق وما بعده { تقدير العزيز } أي الذي لا يغالب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r8.claim: No human can reverse sleep and waking or turn rest into activity, underscoring the force of God's decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p679/r8.anchor: فلو أراد أحد أن يجعل ما جعله من النوم يقظة واليقظة نوما , أو يجعل محل السكن للحركة أو بالعكس أو غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p683/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p683/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p683/r5.claim: The two verses recapitulate the sura's opening: dawn and night are placed first as earlier creations, followed by humanity, created from a single clay-origin and differentiated into all people.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p683/r5.anchor: وكل ذلك مضمون الآيتين في أول السورة , وقدم الإصباح والليل ومتعلقهما لتقدمهما في الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.claim: The account from splitting dawn onward elaborates the earlier statement that God splits grain and kernels, establishing power, oneness, and resurrection before returning to denounce idolatry.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p687/r4.anchor: وكان هذا كله في قوله { فالق الإصباح } شرحا لآية { إن الله فالق الحب والنوى }

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r3.claim: Faliq al-isbah is another predicate of inna; isbah, with a kasra on its first letter, is a verbal noun for entering daylight and names the dawn.

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r4.claim: God splits the dawn's column from the whiteness and spreading light of day.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r4.anchor: أي فالق عمود الفجر عن بياض النهار وإسفاره

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r5.claim: Night is repose because those tired by daytime rest in it, or because creatures dwell in it; the source links this to the wording of Yunus 10:67.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r5.anchor: يسكن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته من سكن إليه إذا اطمأن إليه استئناسا به

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r6.claim: God made the sun and moon follow different cycles that measure time: the sun completes a year and the moon a month, regulating seasons, crops, cultivation, and reproduction.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r6.anchor: على أدوار مختلفة يحسب بها الأوقات فإنه تعالى قدر حركة الشمس بمقدار من السرعة والبطء

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r7.claim: With a ḍamma, hisābān means calculation and counting; with a kasra, hisbān means conjecture and guesswork.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r7.anchor: فالحسبان بالضم مصدر بمعنى الحساب والعد

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r8.claim: Changing lunar phases and new moons let people know debt deadlines and other appointed times, so the sun and moon are instruments for reckoning.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r8.anchor: وباختلاف منازل القمر وتجدد الأهلة في كل شهر يعلم آجال الديون ومواقيت الأشياء

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r9.claim: The sun precedes the moon because of its brightness and its primacy as the source of celestial light; the stars' light is borrowed from it according to their orientation and clarity.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r9.anchor: وتقديم الشمس لضيائها على القمر لأنها معدن الأنوار الفلكية من البدور والنجوم

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r10.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r10.claim: Aftadeh Efendi says the moon's light comes from the realm of lights rather than its own essence; its apparent deficiency results from gradual density, enabling people to know months and years.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r10.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي قدس سره

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r11.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r11.claim: He describes the sun and moon as the very entities of this manifestation, their outward faces directed upward, while their visible inner sides alternately open and close like eyes.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r11.anchor: والشمس والقمر عينا هذا التعين وظاهرهما إلى الفوق والذي نراه جانبهما الداخل

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r12.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r12.claim: He says stars are not embedded in the moon but appear through reflected light in its subtle veins; a shooting star is like the sun moving from place to place, knowledge known to spiritual wayfarers rather than philosophers.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r12.anchor: والكواكب ليست مركوزة فيه وإنما هي بانعكاس الأنوار في بعض عروقه اللطيفة

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r13.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r13.claim: In the afterlife, night and day are not darkness and light but are known by other signs of divine manifestation; one leaf of the referenced tree brought to earth would illuminate the world.
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r13.anchor: الليل والنهار في عالم الآخرة ليسا بالظلمة والضياء بل لهما علامة أخرى بتجلى من التجليات

BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#2/r14.claim: That points to the precise, remarkable reckoning in the sun's and moon's ordered movements.

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r1.claim: The Mighty's determination is His subduing the sun and moon and directing them in their particular courses.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r1.anchor: الذي قهرهما وسيرهما على الوجه المخصوص

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r2.claim: God knows the benefits and interests of the sun and moon for creatures' worldly life and afterlife.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r2.anchor: بما فيهما من المنافع والمصالح المتعلقة بمعاش الخلق ومعادهم

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r3.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r3.claim: Sa'di's Persian poem says clouds, wind, moon, sun, and firmament work so a person can receive bread without heedlessness; they obey God, so it is unfair for a person to disobey.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r3.anchor:
قال السعدي :
ابر وباد ومه وخورشيد وفلك

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses the breaking of dawn as the light of daybreak.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فالق الإصباح} قال: إضاءة الفجر

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as the splitter of daybreak.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فالق الإصباح} قال: فالق الصبح

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the phrase as the one who splits light, the light of daytime.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {فالق الإصباح} قال: فالق النور نور النهار

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r4.claim: Qatāda says every bird and beast settles or rests at night.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وجعل الليل سكنا} قال: يسكن فيه كل طير ودابة

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sun and moon as reckoning the numbers of days, months, and years.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} قال: يعني عدد الأيام والشهور والسنين

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r6.claim: Qatāda says the sun and moon move according to a calculation.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} قال: يدوران في حساب

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r7.claim: Qatāda also glosses ḥusbānan as light or radiance.

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r8.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says the sun and moon follow a reckoning; when their appointed days end, the age ends and the great terror begins.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r8.anchor: عن الربيع في قوله {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} قال: الشمس والقمر في حساب فإذا خلت أيامها فذلك آخر الدهر

DURR-FULL:v3p325/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r9.claim: A report with a weak chain from Ibn ʿAbbās describes a sea beneath the sky, with the sun, moon, and stars running in it; eclipses occur when the sun falls into it, and angels draw it back. The account also describes its nightly course and the angel's release of darkness; it cites 21:33.
DURR-FULL:v3p325/r9.anchor: بسند واه عن ابن عباس قال: خلق الله بحرا دون السماء بمقدار ثلاث فراسخ

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.claim: Muslim ibn Yasār reports a Prophetic prayer asking God, as splitter of dawn and maker of night's repose, to settle debts, relieve poverty, and preserve hearing, sight, and strength for His cause.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.anchor: عن مسلم بن يسار قال: كان دعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم فالق الأصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r1.claim: He glosses the one who splits the dawn as the Creator.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : فالق الاصباح ، يقول : خالق

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r2.claim: He takes al-iṣbāḥ to mean sunlight in the day and moonlight at night.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : فالق الاصباح يعني بالاصباح ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r3.claim: He also explains the phrase as creating night and day.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فالق الاصباح يقول : خالق الليل والنهار

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن مسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r4.claim: He describes the dawn as split away from the night.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن مسلم انه قال : فلق الاصباح عن الليل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r5.claim: He explains it as the illumination of dawn.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد : فالق الاصباح ، اضاءة الفجر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r6.claim: Qatada is reported to give the same dawn-illumination explanation as Mujahid.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r7.claim: He explains it as creating light, the light of day.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك : قوله : فالق الاصباح يقول : خالق النور ، نور النهار

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r8.claim: Night is a repose in which every bird and beast rests.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قول الله : وجعل الليل سكنا ، يسكن فيه كل طير ودابة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r9.speaker: صهيب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r9.claim: Suhayb's wife complained that his long wakefulness harmed him; he replied that night was made a repose for him, but thoughts of Paradise stirred his longing and thoughts of Hell drove away sleep.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r9.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن أبي رواد قال : كان لصهيب امراة فكان يطيل السهر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r10.claim: He says the sun and moon mark the reckoning of days, months, and years.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : والشمس والقمر حسبانا ، يعني عدد الايام والشهور والسنين

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r11.claim: He says the sun and moon revolve according to a reckoning.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1353#2/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : والشمس والقمر حسبانا ، قال : يدوران في حساب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r1.claim: He glosses the sun and moon as light.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r1.anchor: عن قتادة : والشمس والقمر حسبانا ، اي : ضياء

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r2.claim: He explains al-ʿAlīm as being knowledgeable of them.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : العليم يعني عالما بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r8.claim: Faliq al-isbah may be a fourth predicate of inna or an adjective of Allah in the demonstrative clause, leaving the turning-away question parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r8.anchor: { فالق الإصباح } يجوز أن يكون خبرا رابعا عن اسم ( إن ) ، ويجوز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r9.claim: Al-isbah originally names the horizon becoming morning, then the dawn itself: the light of daybreak, opposed to night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r9.anchor: والإصباح بكسر الهمزة في الأصل مصدر أصبح الأفق ، إذا صار ذا صباح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r10.claim: Dawn's appearance is metaphorically pictured as splitting darkness, as in the verse about stripping day from night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r10.anchor: فلق الإصباح استعارة لظهور الضياء في ظلمة الليل ، فشبه ذلك بفلق الظلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r11.claim: The genitive is treated as genuine by the participle's noun-like quality, though its verbal quality also permits a construct; since it describes a past act, its resemblance to an active present participle is weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r11.anchor: لأن اسم الفاعل له شائبة الاسمية فيضاف إضافة حقيقية ، وله شائبة فعلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r12.claim: Alternatively, dawn can be construed as what is split from, with the preposition omitted; night is what is actually cleft, so commentators explain it as splitting the darkness before daybreak, a striking display of power and a boon for life and work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p389/r12.anchor: أي فالق عن الإصباح فانتصب على نزع الخافض ، ولذلك سموا الصبح فلقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r1.claim: The clause about making night a repose is coordinated with the clause about splitting dawn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r1.anchor: { وجاعل الليل سكنا } عطف على { فالق الإصباح }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r2.claim: The majority read ja'il as an active participle and al-layl in the genitive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r2.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بصيغة اسم الفاعل وجر { الليل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r3.speaker: عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r3.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read ja'ala as a past verb and al-layl in the accusative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r3.anchor: وقرأه عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف . { وجعل } بصيغة فعل الماضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r4.claim: Since darkness is absence, God's act here is removing the light that prevents darkness; he apportions the light rather than leaving it constant, so creatures can rest after labor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r4.anchor: وعبر في جانب الليل بمادة الجعل لأن الظلمة عدم فتعلق القدرة فيها هو تعلقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r5.claim: Sakan denotes what one rests in, a metaphorical repose of the soul and reassurance of the heart; here night brings rest from work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r5.anchor: أي تسكن إليه النفس ويطمئن إليه القلب ، والسكون فيه مجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r6.claim: Wives and houses are also called sakan, as in 16:80, because people find repose in them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r6.anchor: وتسمى الزوجة سكنا والبيت سكنا قال تعالى : { والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r7.claim: Sun and moon are accusative by coordination to the syntactic position of al-layl, which functions as the object despite its genitive form; Arabic permits coordination by syntactic case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r7.anchor: وعطف { الشمس والقمر } على { الليل } بالنصب رعيا لمحل الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r8.claim: Hisaban is a verbal noun like ghufran, shukran, and kufran: the sun and moon serve as measures for time, day and night, months, seasons, and years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r8.anchor: والحسبان في الأصل مصدر حسب بفتح السين كالغفران ، والشكران ، والكفران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r9.claim: Many peoples reckon months and years by the sun's passage through the zodiac, while Arabs reckon by lunar stations and Islam uses the lunar calendar; pre-Islamic intercalation aligned years with seasons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r9.anchor: لأن كثيرا من الأمم يحسبون شهورهم وأعوامهم بحساب سير الشمس بحلولها في البروج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r10.claim: The stable, ordered motions of both bodies benefit people beyond religious calendrics and demonstrate divine knowledge and power; deeper knowledge of their system would make the sign still greater.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p391/r10.anchor: وإنما استقام ذلك للناس بجعل الله حركات الشمس والقمر على نظام واحد لا يختلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r1.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means splitting and bringing forth dawn; al-falaq is morning.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r2.claim: The majority read al-iṣbāḥ with kasra on hamza.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وأبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. Abi al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar, and Abu Raja read al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa, plural of ṣubḥ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r4.claim: A group drops tanwīn from fāliq to avoid meeting still consonants and makes al-iṣbāḥ its object; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this anomalous. Sibawayh allows it in poetry, and al-Naḥḥās reports al-Mubarrad allows it in speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r4.anchor: «الإصباح» ب «فالق» كأنه أراد «فالق الإصباح» بتنوين القاف، وهذه قراءة شاذة، وإنما جوز سيبويه مثل هذا في الشعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r5.claim: Sibawayh cites an anonymous verse as poetic evidence for the construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r5.anchor: فألفيته غير مستعتب ... ولا ذاكر الله إلا قليلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة وإبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r6.claim: Abu Ḥaywa, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿī, and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb read falaq al-iṣbāḥ as a past verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وإبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب «فلق الإصباح» بفعل ماض،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-jāʿil al-layl; ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read wa-jaʿala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «وجاعل الليل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r8.claim: The past-tense form aligns fāliq with falaq; accusative sun and moon support it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r8.anchor: وهذا لما كان «فالق» بمعنى الماضي فكأن اللفظ «فلق الإصباح»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r9.claim: The majority read sakanan; Yaʿqūb is reported to read sākinan, but Abu ʿAmr al-Dānī says the report is unsound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «سكنا» وروي عن يعقوب «ساكنا» قال أبو عمرو الداني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r10.claim: With wa-jāʿil, sakanan is accusative through an implied verb because the participle has past force; it means He makes night a rest. Abu ʿAlī says the accusative follows the wording's sense of giving.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r10.anchor: ونصبه بفعل مضمر إذا قرأنا «وجاعل» لأنه بمعنى المضي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r11.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r11.claim: Abu Ḥaywa reads sun and moon in the genitive, coordinated with al-layl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «والشمس والقمر» بالخفض عطفا على لفظ «الليل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r12.claim: Ḥusbān is plural of ḥisāb, like shihbān from shihāb, meaning the bodies run according to calculation, as Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, Qatāda, and Mujāhid say.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r12.anchor: وحسبانا جمع حساب كشهبان في جمع شهاب، أي تجري بحساب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r13.claim: Mujāhid, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, takes ḥusbān as a turning waterwheel and its axle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد في صحيح البخاري المراد حسبان كحسبان إلى حي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r1.claim: The two interpretations of faliq were already given in the commentary on 6:95.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r1.anchor: في معنى الفلق قولان قد سبقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says isbah is the verbal noun of asbaha.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r2.anchor: فأما الإصباح فقال الأخفش هو مصدر من أصبح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says isbah and subh are synonymous.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r4.claim: One view understands isbah as the sun's light by day and the moon's light at night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r4.anchor: أنه ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r5.claim: A second view identifies it as dawn's light; Ibn Zayd describes the break of morning out of night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r5.anchor: أنه إضاءة الفجر قاله مجاهد وقال ابن زيد فلق الإصباح من الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r6.claim: A third view takes isbah as daylight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r6.anchor: والثالث أنه نور النهار قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r7.speaker: أنس بن ماله، الحسن، أبو مجلز، أيوب، الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r7.claim: These readers pronounce the hamza in al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن ماله والحسن وأبو مجلز وأيوب والجحدري فالق الأصباح بفتح الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r8.claim: Abu ʿUbayd explains aṣbāḥ as the plural of ṣubḥ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيد ومعناه جمع صبح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r9.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r9.claim: These readers use jاعil with an alif; Abu ʿAli says this matches faliq by parallel wording.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r9.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر جاعل بألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r10.speaker: عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r10.claim: These readers use jaʿala without an alif and put layl in the accusative; Abu ʿAli takes the participle here as equivalent to the past verb, supported by the following construction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وجعل بغير ألف الليل نصبا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r11.claim: Sakan is what one settles or rests in; people find repose in the night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r11.anchor: فأما السكن فهو ما سكنت إليه والمعنى أن الناس يسكنون فيه سكون راحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r12.speaker: الجمهور، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r12.claim: The majority take husban as calculation; Ibn Qutayba cites the expression for taking each thing according to its calculation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r12.anchor: أحدهما أنه الحساب قاله الجمهور قال ابن قتيبة يقال خذ من كل شيء بحسبانه أي بحسابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r13.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r13.claim: One interpretation of the calculation is that the sun and moon continue moving until their appointed term.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r13.anchor: أنهُما يجريان إلى أجل جعل لهما رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r14.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r14.claim: Another says they move through their stations by calculation and return with increase and decrease.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r14.anchor: يجريان في منازلهما بحساب ويرجعان إلى زيادة ونقصان قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r15.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r15.claim: A third says their courses let people calculate months and years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r15.anchor: أن جريانهما سبب لمعرفة حساب الشهور والأعوام قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r16.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r16.claim: A second lexical view takes husban to mean light or brightness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r16.anchor: والقول الثاني أن معنى الحسبان الضياء قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r17.speaker: الماوردي، ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r17.claim: Al-Mawardi connects the brightness sense to 18:40, where husban means fire; Ibn Jarir rejects the connection as unrelated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p90#2/r17.anchor: قال الماوردي كأنه أخذه من قوله تعالى ﴿ ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء ﴾ أي نارا قال ابن جرير وليس هذا من ذاك في شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r1.claim: God creates light and darkness, splitting night’s darkness at dawn so the world and horizon brighten and night gives way to day; these contrasting creations display His power. The passage links to 6:1 and 7:54.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا} أي: خالق الضياء والظلام، كما قال في أول السورة: {وجعل الظلمات والنور}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r2.claim: Night is calm and dark, a time when things rest; Ibn Kathīr compares the wording with 93:1–2, 92:1–2, and 91:3–4.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r2.anchor: أي: ساجيا مظلما تسكن فيه الأشياء، كما قال: {والضحى والليل إذا سجى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r3.speaker: صهيب الرومي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r3.claim: When his wife reproached him for staying awake, Ṣuhayb al-Rūmī said that night is rest for everyone but him: thoughts of Paradise intensify his longing, and thoughts of Hell drive away sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#2/r3.anchor: وقال صهيب الرومي [رضي الله عنه] (6) لامرأته وقد عاتبته في كثرة سهره: إن الله جعل الليل سكنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r1.claim: The sun and moon move by precise, unvarying calculation through stations in summer and winter, making day and night differ in length.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r1.anchor: يجريان بحساب مقنن مقدر، لا يتغير ولا يضطرب، بل كل منهما له منازل يسلكها في الصيف والشتاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r2.claim: All these motions proceed by the decree of the Almighty, whom none can resist or disobey, and the All-Knowing, from whose knowledge no thing is hidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r2.anchor: فلا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r3.claim: God often closes mentions of night, day, sun, and moon with His might and knowledge, as in the paired verses in Ya Sin and the statement about the lower heaven’s lamps.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p304#3/r3.anchor: وكثيرا ما إذا ذكر الله تعالى خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر، يختم الكلام بالعزة والعلم

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r1.speaker: عاصم، وحمزة، والكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read fāliqi al-iṣbāḥ in an annexation construction and jaʿala al-layla as a past verb.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: فالق الإصباح على الإضافة. وجعل الليل بنصب اللام على فعل ماض

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r2.speaker: باقي القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r2.claim: The other readers have jاعil with alif, an active participle matching fāliق.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون (جاعل) بالألف اتباعا لقوله: (فالق) على أنه اسم الفاعل

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r3.speaker: النخعي
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r3.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads falaqa al-iṣbāḥ and jaʿala without an alif in either, treating both as past verbs.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن النخعي فلق الإصباح (وجعل) بغير ألف فيهما على أنهما فعل ماض

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan is reported with a fatḥa on the hamza of iṣbāḥ.

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan is also reported to read fāliqa with accusative qāf; the usual nominative is coordinated with fāliqi al-ḥabb.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r5.anchor: وعنه: فالق بنصب القاف، والقراء بالرفع على أنه عطف على فالق الحب

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r6.claim: The accusative reading can be understood as an implied 'I mean fāliqa' or as an accusative of glorification.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r6.anchor: فأما النصب فقيل: على تقدير أعني فالق، وقيل: نصب على التعظيم

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r7.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r7.claim: All readers have the accusative coordination 'the sun and moon'; a few read al-qamar in the genitive, coordinated with al-layl.

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r8.claim: Falaq means splitting; it can also mean creation, morning as the darkness splits from it, or a low depression in the land.

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r12.claim: Iṣbāḥ is entering daylight; it is also a verbal noun meaning illumination, while the fatḥa reading means dawns.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r12.anchor: والإصباح: الدخول في ضياء النهار، ومن دخل فيه فهو مصبح

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r13.claim: The word muṣbiḥīn in 15:83 uses the same dawn-root sense of entering daylight.

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r14.claim: Sakan is what one settles or rests toward; a person may be called one's sakan.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r14.anchor: والسكن: الذي يسكن إليه يقال: فلان سكني الذي أسكن إليه

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r15.claim: One explanation takes ḥusbān as a plural of ḥisāb, like shihāb and shuhbān.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r15.anchor: والحسبان: قيل: جمع حساب، كشهاب وشهبان

JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r16.claim: Another explanation makes ḥusbān a verbal noun meaning reckoning, as in the Arab expression for someone's account.
JISHUMI:v3p2330#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: إنه مصدر حسبته حسابا، تقول العرب

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r1.claim: Jaʿil takes two objects because it implies changing something into a new state; fāʿil normally takes one, though jaʿil here means fāʿil.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r1.anchor: جاعل يتعدى إلى مفعولين؛ لأنه يقتضي حالا يصير إليها الشيء خلاف ما كان عليه

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r2.claim: Al-layl is the first object of jaʿil and sakan the second.

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r4.claim: The sun, moon, and ḥusbānan are governed by jaʿil, with an implied 'He made the sun and moon a reckoning.'

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r21.claim: Fāliqu al-iṣbāḥ means splitting the column of dawn from the darkness of night.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r21.anchor: فالق الإصباح أي: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وسواده

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r22.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r22.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk instead glosses it as creator of the morning.

JISHUMI:v3p2331/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r23.claim: God made night a resting time for creation, when every moving creature becomes still, displaying His great care.
JISHUMI:v3p2331/r23.anchor: وقيل: خالق الصباح، عن الضحاك وجعل الليل

JISHUMI:v1p690/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p690/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p690/r1.claim: The recurring arrival and departure of these phenomena prevents harm; their persistence or absence would also cause harm, pointing to a Creator who governs.
JISHUMI:v1p690/r1.anchor: يكن لحصلت المضرة، وكل ذلك يدل على صانع مدبر

JISHUMI:v1p690/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p690/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p690/r2.claim: These signs are singled out because they are both proofs and blessings for people, mentioned after the affirmation of God and visible to everyone.
JISHUMI:v1p690/r2.anchor: لأنها جامعة بين كونها أدلة وكونها نعما على المكلفين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r1.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun used as a name for dawn; with the opening hamza vowel it is also read as a plural meaning mornings.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan reads iṣbāḥ with a fatḥa on the hamza as a plural of ṣubḥ; the cited line uses the word for morning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بفتح الهمزة جمع صبح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r3.claim: The dawn forms with kasra and fatḥa can be verbal nouns; the corresponding evening and morning forms can also be plurals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r3.anchor: بالكسر والفتح مصدرين ، وجمع مساء وصبح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r4.claim: Splitting dawn can mean splitting late-night darkness bordering morning, or splitting dawn itself as its column of light emerges.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r4.anchor: وهي الغبش في آخر الليل ، ومنقضاه الذي يلي الصبح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r5.claim: Dawn is called falaq in the sense of something split open; Arabs describe its column as cleft and split.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r5.anchor: وانصدع الفجر . وسموا الفجر فلقا بمعنى مفلوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭāʾī’s line says blue dawn appears before its white, witnessing the light’s gradual emergence.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r7.claim: One reading has fāliq al-iṣbāḥ and jāʿil al-layl in the accusative as praise; al-Nakhaʿī reads falaq al-iṣbāḥ and jaʿala al-layl.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( فالق الإصباح ، وجاعل الليل سكنا ) بالنصب على المدح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r8.claim: Sakan is what gives a person comfort, such as a spouse or beloved; fire is also called sakan because people enjoy its company.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r8.anchor: السكن : ما يسكن إليه الرجل ويطمئن استئناسا به واسترواحا إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r9.claim: Night calms those exhausted by daytime with rest and renewal; alternatively, it is the time in which people dwell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r9.anchor: والليل يطمئن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته فيه وجمامه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r10.claim: The sun and moon are read in the accusative, genitive, or nominative; the accusative supplies a verb, the genitive coordinates with night, and the nominative begins a clause with an omitted predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r10.anchor: فالنصب على إضمار فعل دل عليه جاعل الليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r11.claim: Night can serve as an object for coordination because the participle’s genitive construction denotes an ongoing act, not a past action.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r11.anchor: ما هو معنى المضي ، وإنما هو دال على جعل مستمر في الأزمنة المختلفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r12.claim: Making the sun and moon ḥusbān means setting them to a calculated course by which people reckon time; ḥusbān is a verbal noun with two vocalizations.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r12.anchor: جعلهما على حسبان ، لأن حساب الأوقات يعلم بدورهما وسيرهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r13.claim: That points to their calculated movement; the Mighty subdues them, and the Knowing governs their courses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p46#2/r13.anchor: إشارة إلى جعلهما حسبانا ، أي ذلك التسيير بالحساب المعلوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r10.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as the one who splits the dawn.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r11.claim: Mujahid explains al-isbah as the light of dawn.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r12.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak explains it as the creator of daylight's light.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r12.anchor: أن معناه خالق نور النهار , وهذا قول الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas takes al-isbah as sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r13.anchor: أن الإصباح ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r14.claim: Night is called a resting place because everything active by day becomes still in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r14.anchor: سمي سكنا لأن كل متحرك بالنهار يسكن فيه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r15.claim: Alternatively, it is a resting place because every living creature takes shelter in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r15.anchor: لأن كل حي يأوي فيه إلى مسكنه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r16.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r16.claim: The sun and moon travel their courses in measured order, with beginning and return and waxing and waning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r16.anchor: يجريان في منازلهما بحساب وبرهان فيه بدء ورد إلى زيادة ونقصان , قاله ابن عباس والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r17.claim: Another view says God made the sun and moon means to know the reckoning of months and years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r17.anchor: أي جعلهما سببا لمعرفة حساب الشهور والأعوام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r18.claim: Qatada interprets the sun and moon as light, drawing an analogy to the word husban for fire in 18:40.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p146/r18.anchor: أي جعل الشمس والقمر ضياء , قاله قتادة , وكأنه أخذه من قوله تعالى

MUJAHID:v1p220#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p220#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p220#2/r1.claim: Faliq al-isbah means the illumination of dawn.

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r7.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means Creator of daylight as its first light appears.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r7.anchor: فقال: { فالق الإصباح } ، يعني خالق النهار من حين يبدوا أوله،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r8.claim: Night is a repose for creatures, when they rest their bodies.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r8.anchor: { وجعل الليل سكنا } لخلقه يسكنون فيه لراحة أجسادهم،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r9.claim: The sun and moon move like a reckoning in their orbits so people can know years and calculate time; God set their stations in the lowest heaven.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r9.anchor: { والشمس والقمر حسبانا } ، يقول: جعلهما في مسيرهما كالحسبان في الفلك، يقول: لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r10.claim: God's setting of these measures is also stated in Yūnus, 10:5.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r10.anchor: فذلك قوله: { ذلك تقدير العزيز } في ملكه يصنع ما أراد، { العليم } [آية: 96] بما قدر من خلقه، نظيرها في يونس.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun used for dawn: God splits the column of morning from night or creates daylight.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r1.anchor: هو مصدر سمى به الصبح أى شاق عمودا صبح عن سواد الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.speaker: كوفي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.claim: The Kufans read jaʿala, coordinating a past-tense verb with fāliq understood as past falaqa.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r2.anchor: وجعل الليل كوفى لأن اسم الفاعل الذى قبله بمعنى المضى فلما كان فالق بمعنى فلق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.claim: Night is a place where creatures rest from the toil of earning a living and sleep.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r3.anchor: مسكونا فيه من قوله لتسكنوا فيه أى ليسكن فيه الخلق عن كد المعيشة إلى نوم الغفلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r4.claim: Night may also quiet estrangement from creation and bring intimacy with the Real.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r4.anchor: أو عن وحشة الخلق إلى الأنس بالحق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r5.claim: The accusative on sun and moon implies a verb supplied from jāʿil: He made the sun and moon.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r5.anchor: انتصبا بإضمار فعل يدل عليه جاعل الليل أى وجعل الشمس والقمر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r6.claim: God made sun and moon move according to reckoning, so their cycles and courses mark the times.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r6.anchor: أى جعلهما على حسبان لأن حساب الأوقات يعلم بدورهما وسيرهما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r7.claim: Ḥusbān with ḍamma is the verbal noun of ḥasaba; with kasra it is the verbal noun of ḥasiba.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r7.anchor: والحسبان بالضم مصدر حسب كما أن الحسبان بالكسر مصدر حسب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r8.claim: Dhālika points to the measured motion of the sun and moon.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى جعلهما حسبانا أى ذلك التسيير بالحساب المعلوم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r9.claim: The mighty God subdued the sun and moon; the knowing God manages and directs them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#2/r9.anchor: ﴿ تقدير العزيز ﴾ الذى قهرهما وسخرهما ﴿ العليم ﴾ بتدبيرهما وتدويرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r1.claim: Faliq al-isbah can qualify God's name, yielding “that is God your Lord, splitter of dawn”; another parsing makes God the subject of a new statement.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r1.anchor: { فالق الإصباح } نعت لاسم الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r2.claim: Ṣubḥ, ṣabāḥ, and iṣbāḥ mean the beginning of day, namely dawn; iṣbāḥ is the verbal noun of aṣbaḥa, and splitting dawn exposes light from darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r2.anchor: والصبح والصباح أول النهار، وكذلك الإصباح أي فالق الصبح كل يوم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r3.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the splitter of dawn as the Creator of daytime.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فالق الإصباح خالق النهار

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r4.claim: Iṣbāḥ is definite and grammarians agree it cannot take nunation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r4.anchor: وهو معرفة لا يجوز فيه التنوين عند أحد من النحويين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r5.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r5.claim: Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read al-asbāḥ with open hamza, as a plural of ṣubḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر «فالق الأصباح» بفتح الهمزة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r6.speaker: الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r6.claim: Al-A'mash transmits from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i the reading falaq al-isbāḥ, on the fa'l pattern, with kasra on hamza and accusative hā.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r6.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي أنه قرأ «فلق الإصباح» على فعل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r7.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r7.claim: Hasan, Isa ibn Umar, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read jaʿala without alif and put al-layl in the accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي «وجعل الليل سكنا» بغير ألف

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r8.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r8.claim: Maki parses accusative al-layl by carrying faliq's sense in both places as a past verb; the later past verbs in 6:97 and 6:99 support the construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r8.anchor: نصب «الليل» حملا على معنى «فالق» في الموضعين لأنه بمعنى فلق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r9.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r9.claim: Maki says the seven canonical readers' unanimous accusative for sun and moon implies an omitted verb, not genitive coordination with fāʿil.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r9.anchor: إجماعهم على نصب الشمس والقمر على إضمار فعل، ولم يحملوه على فاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r10.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب السكوني
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas reports Yazid ibn Qutayb al-Sakuni's reading jaaʿil al-layl sakanan, with sun and moon genitive by coordination on the wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r10.anchor: وقال النحاس: وقد قرأ يزيد بن قطيب السكوني «وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا» بالخفض

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r11.claim: The author clarifies that Maki and al-Mahdawi mean consensus among the seven canonical readers.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r11.anchor: قلت: فيريد مكي والمهدوي وغيرهما إجماع القراء السبع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r12.speaker: يعقوب في رواية رويس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r12.claim: Yaqub, in the transmission of Ruways, reads jaaʿil al-layl sākinan.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r12.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب في رواية رويس عنه «وجاعل الليل ساكنا»

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r13.speaker: أهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r13.claim: The people of Medina read jaaʿil al-layl sakanan, meaning a place of rest.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r13.anchor: وأهل المدينة «وجاعل الليل سكنا» أي محلا للسكون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r14.claim: Yahya ibn Sa'id reports in the Muwatta that the Prophet prayed: splitter of dawn, maker of night for rest, and sun and moon for reckoning; settle my debt and free me from poverty.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r14.anchor: وفي الموطأ عن يحيى بن سعيد أنه بلغه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو فيقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r15.claim: A version in al-Nasa'i, al-Tirmidhi, and others asks that hearing and sight be made the speaker's inheritors.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r15.anchor: وفي كتاب النسائي والترمذي وغيرهما: «واجعله الوارث مني»

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r16.claim: The wording is figurative: the prayer asks that hearing and sight not be taken before the speaker dies.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r16.anchor: في الكلام تجوز، والمعنى: اللهم لا تعدمه قبلي

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r17.claim: The proposed reading that hearing and sight refer to Abu Bakr and Umar is far-fetched; the bodily organs themselves are meant.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r17.anchor: وهذا تأويل بعيد، إنما المراد بهما الجارحتان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r18.claim: Hisāban means by a calculation connected to people's interests.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r18.anchor: ومعنى { حسبانا } أي بحساب يتعلق به مصالح العباد

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the sun and moon's hisāb as calculation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في قوله جل وعز: «والشمس والقمر حسبانا» أي بحساب

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r20.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r20.claim: Al-Akhfash says hisbān is a collective plural of hisāb, like shihāb and shuhbān.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r20.anchor: الأخفش: حسبان جمع حساب مثل شهاب وشهبان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r21.speaker: يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r21.claim: Yaqub analyzes hisbān as a verbal noun of hasaba, while hisāb is the noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r21.anchor: وقال يعقوب: حسبان مصدر حسبت الشيء أحسبه حسبانا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r22.claim: Another view says the sun and moon move by a calculation that neither increases nor decreases, demonstrating God's power and oneness.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r22.anchor: جعل الله تعالى سير الشمس والقمر بحساب لا يزيد ولا ينقص

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r23.claim: Another gloss gives hisbānan the meaning of light.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r24.claim: The author gives a further lexical gloss of hisbān as fire and links the term to 18:40.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96/r24.anchor: والحسبان: النار في لغة وقد قال الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the hasbānan sent from heaven in 18:40 as fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r2.claim: The word hasbāna also denotes a small cushion.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:96#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نارا. والحسبانة: الوسادة الصغيرة

QASHANI:6:95-96/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r4.claim: The dawn is the splitting of the darkness of soul-qualities away from the heart by the rising light of the spirit’s sun.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r4.anchor: فالق ظلمة صفات النفس عن القلب بإصباح نور شمس الروح وإشراقه عليها

QASHANI:6:95-96/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r5.claim: Night is either the soul’s darkness in which the heart sometimes rests and recovers, or the station where bodily faculties settle from agitation.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r5.anchor: ظلمة النفس سكن القلب يسكن إليها للارتفاق والاسترواح أحيانا أو سكنا تسكن فيه القوى البدنية وتستقر عن الاضطراب

QASHANI:6:95-96/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r6.claim: The sun and moon are the spirit and heart, counted among the noble, enduring existents and held in esteem.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r6.anchor: وشمس الروح وقمر القلب محسوبين في عداد الموجودات الباقية الشريفة، معتدا بهما

QASHANI:6:95-96/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r7.claim: Alternatively, the sun and moon are a reckoning or knowledge by which conditions and times are measured.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r7.anchor: أو علمي حسب الأحوال والأوقات تعتبر بهما

QASHANI:6:95-96/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:95-96/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:95-96/r8.claim: God knows the states of disclosure and veiling, alternately manifesting, overpowering, and annihilating the spirit and heart, and acts with wisdom.
QASHANI:6:95-96/r8.anchor: بأحوال البروز والانكشاف والتستر والاحتجاب بهما

RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r1.claim: The verse offers a new proof from celestial phenomena; splitting night with dawn is a greater sign of power and more affecting than the preceding earthly proof from plants and animals.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r1.anchor: فالنوع المتقدم كان مأخوذا من دلالة أحوال النبات والحيوان

RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r2.claim: There are two dawns: the first is a narrow, vertical light like a wolf's tail, followed by full darkness; the second spreads across the horizon.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r2.anchor: فالصبح الأول : هو الصبح المستطيل كذنب السرحان

RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r3.claim: The first, narrow dawn cannot be sunlight: solar light should spread across the horizon and increase continuously, but this dawn appears as a thin line, vanishes into darkness, and is followed by full dawn; God creates it directly, as he creates light and darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p77#3/r3.anchor: علمنا أن ذلك الصبح المستطيل ليس من تأثير قرص الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r1.claim: A body receives light only when it faces the luminous source, a premise philosophers and mathematicians accept; since the sun is below the horizon at dawn, it cannot directly illuminate the ground, so God creates dawn's light.
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r1.anchor: الشمس والقمر وسائر الكواكب لا تقع أضواؤها إلى على الجرم المقابل لها

RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r2.speaker: أبو علي بن الهيثم
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r2.claim: Ibn al-Haytham proposes that the sun below earth lights the opposite air, which successively illuminates adjacent air until the light reaches the atmosphere above us.
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r2.anchor: هذا هو الوجه الذي عول عليه أبو علي بن الهيثم

RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r3.claim: Razi rejects this: transparent, colorless air cannot receive light or color in its substance; if it did, sight would stop at its surface and fail to see what lies beyond, so it could not reflect light onward.

RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r4.speaker: القائلون
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r4.claim: Another objection posits dense vapors and smoke that absorb sunlight and illuminate neighboring air; Razi rejects it because more vapor should strengthen dawn, whereas observation shows the opposite.
RAZI-FULL:v13p78/r4.anchor: فإن قالوا : لم لا يجوز أن يقال

RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r1.claim: Razi's second refutation notes that our horizon is another region's meridian: when the sun is up there at our midnight, it aligns with our eastern air, which still is not illuminated, disproving the claim that air receives and transmits its light.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r1.anchor: إذا وصل مركز الشمس إلى دائرة نصف الليل وتجاوز عنها

RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r2.claim: Even if sunlight causes illumination, bodies share the same essence and extension; any distinguishing property must be a substrate, an inhering quality, or neither, and each option fails, so the sun's special power requires a voluntary creator.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r2.anchor: الأجسام متماثلة في تمام الماهية ومتى كان الأمر كذلك كان حصول هذه الخاصية لقرص الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r1.claim: Since bodies equally admit every property, the sun’s distinctive illumination requires specification by a voluntary agent.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r1.anchor: كل ما يصح على أحد المثلين فإنه يصح أيضا على المثل الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r2.claim: Darkness is deprivation and light pure existence; night brings fear, sleep, and cessation, while dawn restores wakefulness, perception, and movement.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r2.anchor: أن الظلمة شبيهة بالعدم . بل البرهان القاطع قد دل على أنه مفهوم عدمي

RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r3.claim: Because light enables life, sensation, and movement, creating it is among God’s greatest blessings and proofs of power, mercy, and generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r3.anchor: لما كان النور هو السبب الأصلي لحصول هذه الأحوال كان تأثير قدرة الله تعالى في تخليق النور من أعظم أقسام النعم

RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r4.claim: He also reads the dawn splitting figuratively: God brings creation from nonexistence, life and reason from inertness, guidance from ignorance, and spiritual illumination from worldly darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p79#2/r4.anchor: فالق ظلمة العدم بصباح التكوين والإيجاد وفالق ظلمة الجمادية بصباح الحياة والعقل والرشاد

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r1.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r1.claim: Al-Layth defines al-subh, al-sabah, and al-isbah as the beginning of day.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r1.anchor: قال الليث : الصبح والصباح هما أول النهار وهو الإصباح أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r2.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses al-isbah in a line contrasting evening and morning, supporting its sense of morning.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر : أفنى رياحا وبنى رياح … تناسخ الإمساء والإصباح

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r3.claim: A second explanation takes al-isbah as a verbal noun used as a name for morning.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r3.anchor: الإصباح } مصدر سمي به الصبح . فإن قيل : ظاهر الآية يدل

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r4.claim: One explanation supplies an omitted darkness: God splits dawn’s darkness with dawn light, likened to opening a light channel through a sea of darkness in the eastern horizon.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r4.anchor: أن يكون المراد فالق ظلمة الإصباح

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r5.claim: A second explanation is that God splits the morning light to produce the whiteness of day.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r5.anchor: كما يشق بحر الظلمة عن نور الصبح فكذلك يشق نور الصبح عن بياض النهار

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r6.claim: A third explanation names the cause, splitting darkness, while intending its effect, the manifestation of dawn.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r6.anchor: أن ظهور النور في الصباح أنما كان لأجل أن الله تعالى فلق تلك الظلمة

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r7.claim: Some say al-faliq means creator, so the phrase means creator of dawn.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : الفالق هو الخالق فكان المعنى خالق الإصباح

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines sakan as what a person finds reassuring and intimate, such as a spouse or beloved; fire is also called sakan because it offers company, and is called al-muʾnisa.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : السكن ما يسكن إليه الرجل ويطمئن إليه استئناسا به

RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r9.claim: Night provides needed rest after daytime labor, so people can recover from exertion.
RAZI-FULL:v13p80/r9.anchor: ثم إن الليل يطمئن إليه الإنسان لأنه أتعب نفسه بالنهار واحتاج إلى زمان يستريح فيه

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r1.claim: The absence of night in Paradise does not contradict its worldly benefit: the discussion concerns this world’s needs, while its customary conditions do not persist in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r1.anchor: كلامنا في أن الليل والنهار من ضروريات مصالح هذا العالم

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r2.claim: Asim and al-Kisaʾi read wajʿala as a verb; the others read jaʿil as an active participle. The participle suits the preceding active participles, while the verb governs the accusative sun and moon.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r2.anchor: قرأ عاصم والكسائي { وجعل اليل } على صيغة الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r3.claim: The active-participle reading parallels faliq al-habb and faliq al-isbah; the verbal reading supplies a governing verb for the accusative sun and moon.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r3.anchor: حجة من قرأ باسم الفاعل أن المذكور قبله اسم الفاعل

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r4.claim: God set the sun’s cycle to a year and the moon’s to a month, organizing the seasons and the ripening of fruit and harvests; other speeds would disrupt these benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r4.anchor: قدر حركة الشمس مخصوصة بمقدار من السرعة والبطء بحيث تتم الدورة في سنة

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r5.speaker: أبو الهيثم
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r5.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes husban as a plural of hisab, by analogy with other singular and plural pairs.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r5.anchor: قول أبي الهيثم أنه جمع حساب مثل ركاب وركبان وشهاب وشهبان

RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats husban as a verbal noun, noting forms with both damma and kasra and comparing it with words such as kufran and ghufran.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81/r6.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الحسبان بالضم مصدر حسب

RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r1.claim: Making the sun and moon reckoned means setting them to a calculation, since times are known only through their orbits and courses.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r1.anchor: معنى جعل الشمس والقمر حسبانا جعلهما على حساب

RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports three case readings: accusative by an understood verb, genitive coordinated with al-layl, or nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate meaning they are reckoned.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { والشمس والقمر } قرئا بالحركات الثلاث

RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r3.claim: Al-Aziz signals perfect power and al-Alim perfect knowledge: the celestial bodies’ specified properties and measured motions require comprehensive power and knowledge, proving they are specified by a willing agent rather than nature.
RAZI-FULL:v13p81#2/r3.anchor: والعزيز إشارة إلى كمال قدرته والعليم إشارة إلى كمال علمه

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.claim: The cleaving and duality of verses 96–97 continue themes introduced in verse 95.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.anchor: The themes of “cleaving” and duality presented in v. 95 continue in these two verses.

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r2.claim: The first light of dawn appears to split the darkness of night, explaining God’s description as Cleaver of the dawn.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r2.anchor: the first light of dawn seems to cleave or split the darkness of night

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r3.claim: Night as repose is repeatedly presented as a mercy God grants humanity.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r3.anchor: created night for repose is invoked in several places as a mercy God has bestowed upon human beings

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r4.claim: The sun and moon enable temporal reckoning and help determine the direction of the qiblah.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r4.anchor: as is His having created the sun and moon to be useful for reckoning time

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.claim: The Quran groups these celestial bodies in Abraham’s argument and Joseph’s dream.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.anchor: The Quran frequently invokes the sun, moon, and stars together: for example, in Abraham’s argument in vv. 76–78 and in Joseph’s dream

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.claim: The sun, moon, and stars are made subject to God’s command and are described as prostrating to Him.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.anchor: these three kinds of celestial bodies are also described as made subservient by His Command

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.claim: Other verses also describe the celestial bodies as prostrating to God.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.anchor: as prostrating to Him (22:18); see also 55:5–6

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r1.claim: God splits the column of dawn away from the darkness and blackness of night.

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r2.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ is the verbal noun of aṣbaḥnā, “we entered the morning.”

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses al-iṣbāḥ as the morning's illumination.

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses al-iṣbāḥ as the light of dawn.

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses it as the one who splits dawn.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] قال: «فالق الصبح»

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] " يعني بالإصباح: ضوء الشمس بالنهار، وضوء القمر بالليل "

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r7.claim: A second transmission from Mujāhid also glosses it as the splitter of dawn.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد: فالق الإصباح قال: «فالق الصبح»

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd explains it as splitting dawn away from night.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] قال: «فلق الإصباح عن الليل»

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r9.claim: Another report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk calls God the creator of light, the light of day.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r9.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] يقول: «خالق النور، نور النهار»

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to take the phrase as God creating night and day.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: (فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا) يقول: «خلق الليل والنهار»

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r11.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī reportedly read al-iṣbāḥ with fatḥa on the initial alif, construing it as the mornings of successive days.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r11.anchor: عن الحسن البصري أنه كان يقرأ في قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] بفتح الألف

TAB-FULL:v9p426/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts only the kasra reading, citing the consensus of authoritative reciters and exegetes and rejection of the alternative.
TAB-FULL:v9p426/r12.anchor: والقراءة التي لا نستجيز غيرها بكسر الألف {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96]

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that most Hijazi and Medinan readers and some Basrans read jāʿil as an active participle; his syntactic example shows coordination by meaning.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r1.anchor: قعودا لدى الأبواب طلاب حاجة … عوان من الحاجات أو حاجة بكرا

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r2.claim: In that reading al-layl is genitive by annexation but accusative in syntactic position as jāʿil's object; sun and moon are coordinated with that underlying object position.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r2.anchor: قعودا لدى الأبواب طلاب حاجة … عوان من الحاجات أو حاجة بكرا

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r3.claim: A cited poetic line coordinates the second “need” in the accusative with the first by meaning rather than its genitive form.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r3.anchor: قعودا لدى الأبواب طلاب حاجة … عوان من الحاجات أو حاجة بكرا

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r4.claim: A second poetic example illustrates coordination by the preceding meaning even without an intervening word.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r4.anchor: فبينا نحن ننظره أتانا … معلق شكوة وزناد راع

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r5.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r5.claim: Most Kufan reciters read jaʿala as a past-tense verb, with al-layl in the accusative.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r5.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفيين: {وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس} [الأنعام: 96] على (فعل) بمعنى الفعل الماضي

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both widespread readings as sound in grammar and meaning.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r6.anchor: إنهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار، متفقتا المعنى غير مختلفتيه

TAB-FULL:v9p427/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r7.claim: God made night a repose because things active by day grow quiet and settle in their dwelling places at night.
TAB-FULL:v9p427/r7.anchor: لأنه يسكن فيه كل متحرك بالنهار، ويهدأ فيه فيستقر في مسكنه ومأواه

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the sun and moon as reckoning the days, months, and years.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} [الأنعام: 96] يعني: «عدد الأيام والشهور والسنين»

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the sun and moon run until an appointed term.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} [الأنعام: 96] قال: «يجريان إلى أجل جعل لهما»

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the sun and moon have a reckoning; when their days expire, the age ends and the great terror begins.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} [الأنعام: 96] قال: " الشمس والقمر في حساب، فإذا خلت أيامهما فذاك آخر الدهر، وأول الفزع الأكبر

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r5.claim: Qatāda says they revolve according to a reckoning.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} [الأنعام: 96] قال: «يدوران في حساب»

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r6.claim: Mujāhid connects the phrase with the sun and moon moving in their orbits, as in 21:33 and 55:5.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد: {والشمس والقمر حسبانا} [الأنعام: 96] قال: " هو مثل قوله: {كل في فلك يسبحون} [الأنبياء: 33] ، ومثل قوله: و {الشمس والقمر بحسبان} [الرحمن: 5]

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r7.claim: A second report from Qatāda glosses ḥusbānan as light.

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r8.speaker: author
