TAB-FULL:v9p429/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers reckoned motion through appointed limits for the creatures' benefit, rather than the alternative “light.”
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r8.anchor: وجعل الشمس والقمر يجريان بحساب وعدد لبلوغ أمرهما ونهاية آجالهما، ويدوران لمصالح الخلق التي جعلا لها

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r9.claim: The context favors measured motion because dawn's illumination was already mentioned, so repeating that sense here would add nothing.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r9.anchor: لأنه قد وصف ذلك قبل قوله: {فالق الإصباح} [الأنعام: 96] ، فلا معنى لتكريره مرة أخرى في آية واحدة

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r10.claim: In Arabic ḥusbān can be the plural of ḥisāb, analogous to shuhbān from shihāb, or a verbal noun meaning reckoning.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r10.anchor: والحسبان في كلام العرب: جمع حساب، كما الشهبان جمع شهاب، وقد قيل: إن الحسبان في هذا الموضع مصدر

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r11.claim: With kasra on ḥāʾ, ḥusbān is a plural of ḥasbāna, a small cushion, unrelated to the other senses.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r11.anchor: وأما (الحسبان) بكسر الحاء، فإنه جمع الحسبانة: وهي الوسادة الصغيرة

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r12.claim: In 18:40 Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly glosses ḥusbānan min al-samāʾ as fire; al-Ṭabarī says that sense does not apply here.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء} [الكهف: 40] ، قال: نارا

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r13.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r13.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects carrying the fire sense from 18:40 into this verse.
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r13.anchor: وليس هذا من ذلك المعنى في شيء

TAB-FULL:v9p429/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r14.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p429/r14.claim: The accusative ḥusbānan is governed by jaʿala; a Basran analysis treats it as “by a reckoning,” with bi omitted as in 6:117.

SULAMI:v1p209#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r1.claim: God splits open hearts through the spreading of lights from the unseen.
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : فالق القلوب بشرح أنوار الغيوب

SULAMI:v1p209#7/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r2.claim: God illuminates the innermost secrets with the light of gnosis.
SULAMI:v1p209#7/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : منور الأسرار بنور المعرفة

AKHFASH:v1p307/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p307/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p307/r1.claim: الإصباح is the verbal noun of أصبح; another form, الأصباح, is used as a collective for mornings.
AKHFASH:v1p307/r1.anchor: جعله مصدرا من "أصبح". وبعضهم يقول {فالق الأصباح} جماع "الصبح"

AKHFASH:v1p307/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p307/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p307/r2.claim: حسبانا means by calculation, with ب omitted; حسبان is a collective of حساب, as شهبان is of شهاب, and 55:5 states the same idea with بحسبان.
AKHFASH:v1p307/r2.anchor: أي: بحساب. فحذف الباء كما حذفها من قوله {أعلم من يضل عن سبيله}

TABRISI:6:95-96/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة
TABRISI:6:95-96/r1.claim: Readers in Kufa read wa-jaʿala al-layla sakanan; the other readers read wa-jāʿilu, with al-layli in the genitive.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وجعل الليل سكنا والباقون وجاعل بالألف والرفع الليل بالجر

TABRISI:6:95-96/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:6:95-96/r2.claim: The participial reading coordinates jāʿil with the preceding participle fāliqu, since nouns more naturally coordinate with nouns; cited poetry similarly uses an implied verbal noun.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r2.anchor: للبس عباءة وتقر عيني أحب إلي من لبس الشفوف

TABRISI:6:95-96/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r3.speaker: أهل الكوفة
TABRISI:6:95-96/r3.claim: The perfect-tense reading treats fāliqu as past in meaning, so it coordinates with a verb; the following accusative sun and moon likewise reflect an implied verb.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ أو جعل فلأن اسم الفاعل الذي قبله بمعنى المضي فلما كان فاعل بمعنى فعل عطف عليه فعل

TABRISI:6:95-96/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r6.claim: Iṣbāḥ and ṣubḥ both mean morning; iṣbāḥ is the verbal noun of becoming morning.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r6.anchor: والإصباح والصبح واحد وهو مصدر أصبحنا إصباحا

TABRISI:6:95-96/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:95-96/r7.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to read fāliqu al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa, meaning the dawn of each day; no one else is reported with this reading.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r7.anchor: وقد روي عن الحسن أنه قرأ فالق الأصباح بالفتح يريد صبح كل يوم

TABRISI:6:95-96/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r8.claim: Sakan is that in which one settles and rests.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r8.anchor: والسكن الذي يسكن إليه والحسبان جمع حساب

TABRISI:6:95-96/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r9.claim: Ḥusbān can be a plural of ḥisāb or a verbal noun; it also has other Arabic uses, including a small cushion and verbal nouns for reckoning or considering someone intelligent.
TABRISI:6:95-96/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر حسبت الحساب أحسبه حسابا وحسبانا وحكي عن بعض العرب

TABRISI:6:95-96/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96/r10.claim: The accusative sun and moon are objects of an implied jaʿala; the participle jāʿil cannot govern the past-time object when annexed to the following noun, like “striking Zayd yesterday.”
TABRISI:6:95-96/r10.anchor: النصب في الشمس والقمر مفعول فعل يدل عليه قوله وجاعل الليل سكنا وتقديره وجعل الشمس والقمر حسبانا

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r8.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r8.claim: Most exegetes explain fāliqu al-iṣbāḥ as splitting the column of dawn out of the dark night.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r8.anchor: { فالق الإصباح } أي شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وسواده عن أكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas alternatively says it means creating the morning.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه خالق الصباح عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and most exegetes say God made night a time for rest and dwelling; night is for repose and day for activity, and their alternation shows His power and wisdom.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r10.anchor: { وجاعل الليل سكنا } تسكنون فيه وتتودعون فيه عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي وقتادة ومجاهد
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Suddi, Qatada, and Mujahid say the sun and moon follow calculated orbits: the sun completes twelve zodiacal signs in 365¼ days and the moon its cycle in 28 days, ordering nights, days, months, and years.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r11.anchor: { والشمس والقمر حسبانا } أي جعلهما تجريان في أفلاكهما بحساب لا يتجاوزانه حتى ينتهيا إلى أقصى منازلهما

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r12.claim: Their calculation benefits people’s transactions, dating, worship times, and other religious and worldly affairs.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r12.anchor: أشار سبحانه بذلك إلى ما في حسابهما من مصالح العباد في معاملاتهم وتواريخهم وأوقات عباداتهم

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r13.claim: The verse is linked to 55:5, which says the sun and moon follow calculation, and 21:33, which says each swims in an orbit.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r13.anchor: والشمس والقمر بحسبان [الرحمن: 5] وقال كل في فلك يسبحون [الأنبياء: 33]

TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r14.claim: That points to the dawn’s splitting, night’s role as rest, and the calculated sun and moon; it is the ordering of the invincible God, who knows His creatures’ interests and how to govern them.
TABRISI:6:95-96#2/r14.anchor: { ذلك } إشارة إلى ما وصفه سبحانه من فلق الأصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا:

THALABI:v4p171#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r5.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means splitting the column of dawn from night’s darkness and revealing it.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r5.anchor: فالق الإصباح شاق عمود الصبح من ظلمة الليل وكاشفه.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v4p171#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the phrase as the creator of daytime.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: خالق النهار، والأصباح مصدر كالإقبال والإدبار

THALABI:v4p171#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r7.claim: Iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun meaning illumination, like iqbāl and idbār.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r7.anchor: والأصباح مصدر كالإقبال والإدبار وهي الإضاءة.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r8.speaker: الحسن والقيسي
THALABI:v4p171#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Qaysi read al-iṣbāḥ with an open hamza, treating it as a plural like qurs/aqrāṣ.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والقيسي: فالق الإصباح بفتح الهمزة جعله جمع مثل قرص وأقراص.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r9.speaker: النخعي
THALABI:v4p171#2/r9.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi reads both clauses as past-tense verbs.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ النخعي: فلق الأصباح وجعل الليل سكنا.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r10.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v4p171#2/r10.claim: The Kufans read both clauses as verbs, following the codex’s consonantal text.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا على الفعل اتباعا للمصحف.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r11.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v4p171#2/r11.claim: The other readers use the noun forms in both clauses.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: كلاهما بالألف على الإسم.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r12.claim: Night is a repose in which God’s creatures dwell.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r12.anchor: وجاعل الليل سكنا سكن فيه خلقه.

THALABI:v4p171#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r13.claim: The sun and moon follow a measured reckoning and reach the limits of their courses without passing beyond it.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r13.anchor: والشمس والقمر حسبانا أي جعل الشمس والقمر بحساب لا يجاوزاه

THALABI:v4p171#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r14.speaker: يزيد بن قعنب
THALABI:v4p171#2/r14.claim: Yazid ibn Quʿnib reads al-shams wa-al-qamar in the genitive, conjoined to the preceding word by its form.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ [يزيد بن قعنب] : والشمس والقمر بالخفض عطفا على اللفظ،

THALABI:v4p171#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171#2/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171#2/r15.claim: Ḥusbān can be a verbal noun like nuqṣān or a plural of ḥisāb like shihāb/shuhbān and rikāb/rukbān.
THALABI:v4p171#2/r15.anchor: والحسبان مصدر كالنقصان والرحمان وقد يكون جمع حساب مثل شهاب وشهبان، وركاب وركبان.

THALABI:v4p172/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p172/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p172/r1.claim: The ordering of dawn, night, sun, and moon is the decree of the Mighty and Knowing God.
THALABI:v4p172/r1.anchor: ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم أي خلقها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r1.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r1.claim: Al-Iṣbāḥ is the verbal noun of falaqa yafluqu; Ibn al-Sikkit records the expression samitu dhālika min falq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r1.anchor: سمعت ذاك من فلق (¬4) فيه، ذكره ابن السكيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r2.speaker: الليث والفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r2.claim: They define iṣbāḥ as dawn or the beginning of day; a poetic line about evening and morning provides usage evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r2.anchor: قال الليث (¬6): (الصبح والصباح هما أول النهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r3.claim: He cites an anonymous line using iṣbāḥ for morning, paired with evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r3.anchor: أفنى رياحا وذوى رياح ... تناسخ الإمساء والإصباح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r4.speaker: كثير من أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r4.claim: Many commentators say dawn's shaft is split out of the darkness; the author rejects the direction, saying night splits for dawn, not dawn for night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r4.anchor: فقال كثير من أهل التفسير في قوله {فالق الإصباح}: (شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وسواده)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والمحققون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exacting commentators explain God as creating a new dawn each day; al-Kalbi gives the same explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r5.anchor: ابن عباس (¬2) والمحققون (¬3) قالوا: {فالق الإصباح} أي: خالق الإصباح كل يوم جديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq allows either creator of dawn or one who brings dawn forth; both readings ultimately return to creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: {فالق الإصباح}: (جائز أن يكون خالق الإصباح، وجائز أن يكون معناه: سياق الإصباح، وهو راجع إلى معنى خالق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq explains falaq in Surat al-Falaq as creation, noting that much of creation comes through splitting; the author connects this to 6:95.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r7.anchor: وقال في سورة الفلق: (الفلق الخلق، وإذا تأملت الخلق تبين لك أن أكثره عن انفلاق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r8.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r8.claim: Al-Layth says God originated and clarified the dawn; the author therefore takes fāliq as bringing forth and making clear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p304/r8.anchor: قال الليث: (الله تعالى فلق الصبح، أي: أبدأه وأوضحه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r1.claim: Sakan means what one settles toward; God made night a repose in which people rest.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r1.anchor: السكن: معناه في اللغة ما سكنت إليه، يريد: أن الناس يسكنون في الليل سكون الراحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says every living creature rests during the night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: أن كل ذي روح يسكن فيه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says creatures rest at night and return to their homes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (يسكن فيه الخلق ويرجعوا إلى أوطانهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r4.claim: He connects this wording to the verse saying God made night so people may rest in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r4.anchor: هو (¬5) الذى جعل لكم اليل لتسكنوا فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r5.claim: Most readers read jāʿil with an alif, matching the preceding active participles and favoring a noun coordinated with a noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r5.anchor: فقرأ الأكثرون (جاعل) بالألف؛ لأن قبله اسم فاعل وهو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r6.speaker: أهل الكوفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r6.claim: The Kufans read jaʿala as a past verb because the preceding active participle carries past meaning; the following accusative sun and moon support that analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p307/r6.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة {وجعل الليل} لأن اسم الفاعل الذي قبله بمعنى الماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ḥusbānan as calculation, like the wording in 10:5 about knowing the number of years and reckoning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the sun and moon move through measured phases without exceeding them until reaching their furthest stations.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r3.claim: Qatada says the sun and moon revolve according to a calculation; the report is transmitted by Shayban.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r3.anchor: وروى شيبان (¬5) عن قتادة قال: ([يدوران] (¬6) في حساب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash takes ḥusbānan as bi-ḥisāb with the preposition omitted, estimating that the sun and moon run according to calculation, as in 17:61.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r4.anchor: عن الأخفش أنه قال: (معناه: بحساب، فحذف الباء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r5.speaker: ثعلب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r5.claim: Thaʿlab treats ḥusbānan as a verbal noun, like ḥasibtuhu aḥsubuhu ḥusbānan and ḥisāban.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r5.anchor: وقال ثعلب: ({حسبانا} مصدر كما تقول: حسبته أحسبه حسبانا وحسابا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r6.claim: Abu Zayd's poetic example uses ḥusbānī to mean reckoning or calculation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r6.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيد عن أبي زيد: على الله حسباني إذا النفس أشرفت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r7.speaker: الأخفش وأبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r7.claim: They analyze ḥusbān as a plural of ḥisāb, analogous to rukbān from rikāb and shuhbān from shihāb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r7.anchor: وهو قول أبي الهيثم (¬8) قال: (الحسبان جمع حساب مثل: ركاب وركبان، وشهاب وشهبان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad give the same plural analysis for 55:5; those who take ḥusbān as a verbal noun compare it to rajḥān and nuqṣān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r8.anchor: وهو قول أبي عبيدة (¬1) والمبرد (¬2) ذكرا ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r9.claim: They explain the accusative as coordinated with the meaning of jāʿil, which contains jaʿala; the analysis also explains the accusative sakana.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r9.anchor: فأما نصب {الشمس والقمر} فقال أبو إسحاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r10.claim: Al-Farra treats night as accusative in sense, so the sun and moon follow its meaning; genitive is preferred without an intervening phrase, though accusative is possible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: (الليل في قوله (وجاعل الليل) في موضع نصب في المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p308/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains that Arabic can coordinate an accusative after a genitive by treating the first noun as accusative in meaning, illustrated by the quoted line.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r1.claim: The line beginning baynā naḥnu is cited in this discussion of accusative coordination and its interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r1.anchor: فنبينا نحن ننظره أتانا ... معلق شكوة وزناد راع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also explains the reverse pattern, where a genitive follows an accusative by construing the first item as genitive; he cites Imruʾ al-Qays.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r2.anchor: وقال امرئ القيس: فظل طهاة اللحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God determined the provisions of each era and what is suitable for it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: الذي قدر الأقوات في كل زمان وما يصلح فيه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r4.claim: The commentators gloss al-Aziz as sovereign who does whatever He wills, and al-Alim as knowing what He determined in creating the sun and moon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p311/r4.anchor: وقال المفسرون: (يعني: {العزيز}: في ملكه يصنع ما أراد، {العليم}: بما قدر من خلقهما)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r1.claim: God splits the column of dawn from the darkness of night, meaning that He creates and brings dawn into being.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r1.anchor: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل وسواده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r2.claim: God made night a resting place where creatures sleep in repose.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r3.claim: The sun and moon move according to a reckoning and do not exceed the limits of their calculated courses.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r3.anchor: وجعل الشمس والقمر بحسبان لا يجاوزانه فيما يدوران في حساب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r4.claim: This is the measure of the Mighty, who acts as He wills in His dominion, and the All-Knowing of what He has measured in creating them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:96/r4.anchor: في ملكه يصنع ما أراد { العليم } بما قدر من خلقهما

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.claim: His rendering describes God as splitting grains and kernels, bringing life from death and death from life, splitting dawn, making night a resting place, and setting the sun and moon for reckoning.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r1.anchor: Allah o dâneleri, çekirdekleri pörtleten, ölüden diri çıkarır ve diriden ölü çıkaran

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.claim: After establishing that none escapes God’s power, Elmalılı points to his splitting darkness to bring dawn as further evidence of that power.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r13.anchor: Gerek hayatta olun gerek mematta, gerek hayvanlara karışın gerek otlara, gerek yere geçin gerek göğe çıkın

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r14.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means splitting the darkness to make dawn and bring out light.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r14.anchor: sabahı çatlatan, zulmetleri yarıp fecr yapan, ziyâyı aksettirip tan attıran O’dur.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r15.claim: God makes night a quiet setting for rest, veiling the day’s activity so excitement subsides and fatigue can ease.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r15.anchor: O geceyi seken, dinlenecek, istirahat edecek bir muhît-i sükûn

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r16.claim: He notes that this wording is read by reciters other than Asim, Hamza, Kisa’i, and Khalaf al-Ashir.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r16.anchor: Âsım, Hamza, Kisâî ve Halef-i Âşir’den mâ‘adâsında وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ سَكَنًۭا okunur.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r17.claim: The sun and moon are not agents of day and night but instruments marking reckoning; their movements and the cycles of activity and rest are measured.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r17.anchor: Âyet-i nehâr olan Şems ve âyet-i leyl olan Kamer bunların âmil ve fâ‘ili değil, vâsıta-i hisâbiyeleridir.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r18.claim: God determined quantities, created reckoning, and made the sun and moon signs by which people account for their activity and rest, for which they are responsible.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r18.anchor: Allah teâlâ mekādîr ve kemmiyâtı ta‘yîn ü tahsis ederek hesabı da halk etmiş, Şems ve Kamer’i bu hareket ü sükûnun hisâbına birer alâmet yapmıştır.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r19.claim: The calibrated order of opposed possibilities and forces reflects the exact measure of the Mighty, All-Knowing God, not chance or a blind nature.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r19.anchor: Ne hesabsız, takdirsiz, gelişigüzel, keyfemettefak oluvermiş bir tesadüftür ne de ne yaptığını bilmeyen kör bir tabiatın ıttırâdıdır.

ELMALILI:6:95-96/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r20.claim: God’s power is unmatched and independent of nature; worshipping natural, vital, or celestial forces under his authority cannot free anyone from his reckoning.
ELMALILI:6:95-96/r20.anchor: u fâtır olan Allah yalnız kādir değil, şerîk ve nazîri yok bir Azîz ü Alîm’dir de.

MAJAZ:v1p201/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p201/r1.claim: Al-shams and al-qamar are accusative: sakana separates them from al-layl’s genitive link to jāʿil, so the verb governing sakana also governs them; al-Farazdaq supplies a parallel.
MAJAZ:v1p201/r1.anchor: وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر» (96) منصوبتين، لأنه فرق بينهما وبين الليل المضاف إلى جاعل قوله: «سكنا»

MAJAZ:v1p201/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p201/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p201/r2.claim: Ḥusbānan is a collective of ḥisāb, on the pattern of shihāb with plural shihbān.
MAJAZ:v1p201/r2.anchor: والشمس والقمر حسبانا» (96) ، وهو جميع حساب، فخرج مخرج شهاب، والجميع شهبان.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:96/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:96/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:96/r1.claim: Dawn, tranquil night, and the sun and moon’s mathematically regular cycles enable timekeeping and other astronomical and geographical measures; all are God’s ordering.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:96/r1.anchor: ay ve güneşin şaşmaz bir matematiksel nisbetle, insanların zamanı ve daha başka astronomik ve coğrafî ölçüleri bulmalarına imkân verecek düzenlilikle işlevlerini sürdürmeleri de o azîz ve alîm olan Allah’ın takdiridir

BAQILLANI:v1p179/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r1.claim: The ode under discussion ranges from commonplace and weak lines to obscure, unpleasant ones and a few counted as excellent.
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r1.anchor: قد ترددت بين أبيات سوقية مبتذله وأبيات متوسطة وأبيات ضعيفة مرذولة وأبيات وحشية غامضة مستكرهة

BAQILLANI:v1p179/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r2.claim: Obscure, shocking verse that obstructs understanding and defeats the purpose of communication should be classed with riddles, not eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r2.anchor: ولا يقع بمثله التمدح والتفاصح وهو مجانب لما وضع له أصل الإفهام ومخالف لما بني عليه التفاهم

BAQILLANI:v1p179/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda explains that the woman does not gird herself to work but lounges in luxury; here عن means after.
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r3.anchor: وعن هي بمعنى بعد قال أبو عبيدة لم تنتطق فتعمل ولكنها تتفضل

BAQILLANI:v1p179/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r4.claim: Some preferred Imru al-Qays's night imagery over al-Nabigha's: its breast, back, and flanks make night seem heavy and slow to retreat, unlike Abu Tammam's remote metaphors.
BAQILLANI:v1p179/r4.anchor: فقدمت أبيات امرئ القيس واستحسنت استعارتها وقد جعل لليل صدرا يثقل تنحيه ويبطئ تقضيه

BAQILLANI:v1p187/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r1.claim: The Qur'anic arrangement can unite unlike phrases more delicately than naturally matched speech, as the author illustrates with 42:53.
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r1.anchor: قد صيرهما شريف النظم أشد ائتلافا من الكلام المؤالف وألطف انتظاما من الحديث الملائم

BAQILLANI:v1p187/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r2.claim: In 6:96, four individually splendid phrases combine to display God's power and command, joining fluidity with firmness and beauty with strength.
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r2.anchor: أنظر إلى هذه الكلمات الأربع التي ألف بينها واحتج بها على ظهور قدرته ونفاذ أمره

BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.claim: Every Qur'anic word can carry complete eloquence on its own, yet gains further beauty and instruction in composition; these verses exceed familiar speech and human ability.
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r3.anchor: فإذا كانت الآية تنتظم من البديع وتتألف من البلاغات فكيف لا تفوت حد المعهود ولا تحوز شأو المألوف

BAQILLANI:v1p187/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r4.claim: A full sūra should be examined word by word, with attention to its stories and proofs; he points readers to Sūrat al-Naml for this analysis.
BAQILLANI:v1p187/r4.anchor: ثم اقصد إلى سورة تامة فتصرف في معرفة قصصها وراع ما فيها من براهينها وقصصها

BURHAN:v4p110/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p110/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p110/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows الشمس to coordinate with the syntactic position of الليل.
BURHAN:v4p110/r7.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أيضا في قوله تعالى

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r1.claim: Iqtibās embeds Qurʾanic wording in prose or poetry without explicitly attributing it to God; the Mālikīs are widely reported to prohibit it.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r1.anchor: الاقتباس تضمين الشعر أو النثر بعض القرآن لا على أنه منه بألا يقال فيه قال الله تعالى ونحوه

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r2.speaker: عز الدين ابن عبد السلام
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r2.claim: ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām permitted iqtibās, citing the Prophet’s use in prayer and elsewhere, including a supplication echoing this verse.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r2.anchor: فسئل عنه الشيخ عز الدين ابن عبد السلام فأجازه واستدل له بما ورد عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم من قوله في الصلاة وغيرها

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r3.claim: The cited evidence supports iqtibās in admonition, praise, supplication, and prose; al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr considers poetic use disliked but prose permissible.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r3.anchor: وهذا كله إنما يدل على جوازه في مقام الموعظ والثناء والدعاء وفي النثر لا دلالة فيه على جوازه في الشعر

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r4.speaker: القاضي عياض
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ used Qurʾanic iqtibās in prose passages of his al-Shifāʾ sermon.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r4.anchor: واستعمله أيضا في النثر القاضي عياض في مواضع من خطبة الشفا

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r5.speaker: الشرف إسماعيل بن المقرئ
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r5.claim: Al-Sharaf Ismāʿīl ibn al-Muqriʾ accepts iqtibās in sermons, admonitions, and praise of the Prophet, even in verse, and rejects other uses.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r5.anchor: وقال الشرف إسماعيل بن المقرئ اليمني صاحب مختصر الروضة في شرح بديعيتة ما كان منه في الخطب والمواعظ ومدحه صلى الله عليه وسلم ولو في النظم فهو مقبول

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r6.speaker: ابن حجة
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r6.claim: Ibn Ḥijja divides iqtibās into accepted use in sermons, admonitions, and covenants; permitted use in speech, letters, and stories; and rejected misuse.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r6.anchor: وفي شرح بديعية ابن حجة الاقتباس ثلاثة أقسام مقبول ومباح ومردود

ITQAN:v1p296#3/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r7.speaker: ابن حجة
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r7.claim: Rejected misuse includes transferring God’s first-person words to oneself, as in the Marwānid example, or inserting a verse for humor.
ITQAN:v1p296#3/r7.anchor: والثالث على ضربين أحدهما ما نسبه الله إلى نفسه ونعوذ بالله ممن ينقله إلى نفسه

DAMGHANI:v1p240/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r14.claim: Sakan can mean a place of rest and quiet; night is where people rest from fatigue.
DAMGHANI:v1p240/r14.anchor: فوجه منها : التسكين بمعنى القرار قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r10.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ means dawn and is originally a verbal noun; sakan is what one rests in, and ḥusbān means reckoning or calculation.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r10.anchor: الإصباح بكسر الهمزة هو الصبح وهو في الأصل مصدر، والسكن ما يسكن إليه، والحسبان جمع حساب

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r11.claim: The verbal clause about making night a repose is coordinated with the nominal clause about dawn; this is sound because the latter conveys an action. A reading has وجاعل.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r11.anchor: ولا ضير في عطف الجملة الفعلية على الاسمية إذا اشتملت على معنى الفعل وقرئ { وجاعل }

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r12.claim: Night lets moving things rest, renew their strength, and recover from the fatigue and weariness of daytime activity.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r12.anchor: يسكن فيه المتحركات عن حركاتها لتجديد القوى ودفع ما عرض لها من التعب والعي والكلال

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r13.claim: The sun and moon's motions mark days, nights, months, and years, providing a remarkable measure that orders human livelihood and life.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r13.anchor: وجعل الشمس والقمر بما يظهر من الليل والنهار والشهور والسنين من حركاتهما

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r14.claim: God is invincible in His governance and knows every interest of His dominion, so His ordering does not fail or decay by itself.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r14.anchor: فهو العزيز الذي لا يقهره قاهر فيفسد عليه شيئا من تدبيره، والعليم الذي لا يجهل بشيء من مصالح مملكته

TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r4.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن بنت إلياس
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r4.claim: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Bint Ilyas reports from al-Rida that God made night and women sources of repose; the Sunnah includes marrying at night and feeding people.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي بن بنت إلياس قال سمعت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام يقول إن الله جعل الليل سكنا

TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r5.speaker: علي بن عقبة
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r5.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿUqba reports from his father and al-Sadiq: marry at night because God made it repose, and do not seek one’s needs at night.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#14/r5.anchor: عن علي بن عقبة عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال تزوجوا بالليل فإن الله جعله سكنا

BURHAN:v1p481/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.claim: Al-ʿIzz cites prophetic supplications and speech, along with the letter to Heraclius and Ibn ʿUmar's wording, as precedents for using Qur'anic language outside recitation and with altered wording.
BURHAN:v1p481/r2.anchor: ورد عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وجهت وجهي والتلاوة

ITQAN:v2p310/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p310/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p310/r13.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ refers to sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
ITQAN:v2p310/r13.anchor: 1609 ﴿ فالق الإصباح ﴾ ضوء الشمس بالنهار وضوء القمر بالليل

ITQAN:v2p310/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p310/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p310/r14.claim: Ḥusbānan means the counting of days, months, and years.

FARRA:v1p345/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r9.claim: الإصباح is the verbal noun of أصبحنا إصباحا and denotes the whole of each day's morning.
FARRA:v1p345/r9.anchor: والإصباح مصدر أصبحنا إصباحا، والإصباح صبح كل يوم بمجموع

FARRA:v1p345/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r10.claim: الليل is accusative in sense, and الشمس والقمر follow its sense because سَكَنًا interrupts them; without an intervening word, genitive coordination is preferred.
FARRA:v1p345/r10.anchor: الليل في موضع نصب في المعنى. فرد الشمس والقمر على معناه

FARRA:v1p345/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r11.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v1p345/r11.claim: An anonymous line shows accusative coordination can also occur without an intervening word, though Farrāʾ says the interruption is preferable.
FARRA:v1p345/r11.anchor: وقد يجوز أن ينصب وإن لم يحل بينهما بشيء أنشد بعضهم:

FARRA:v1p345/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r12.claim: The second noun may be genitive despite tanwīn on the first when both mean the same construction; Farrāʾ prefers placing an intervening element, citing Imruʾ al-Qays.
FARRA:v1p345/r12.anchor: وتقول: أنت آخذ حقك وحق غيرك فتضيف في الثاني

NAHHAS:v2p82/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r14.claim: Fāliq is definite and adjectival; all grammarians except al-Kisai reject tanwīn here.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r14.anchor: نعت وهو معرفة لا يجوز فيه التنوين عند أحد من النحويين

NAHHAS:v2p82/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r15.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means the one who splits open dawn; Arabic also calls dawn falaq al-ṣubḥ and farq al-ṣubḥ.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r15.anchor: ومعنى فالق الإصباح الذي خلق له فلقا وهو الفجر

NAHHAS:v2p82/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r16.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
NAHHAS:v2p82/r16.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa on the hamza, treating it as a plural of ṣubḥ.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r16.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر ( فالق الأصباح ) بفتح الهمزة

NAHHAS:v2p82/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r17.speaker: الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي
NAHHAS:v2p82/r17.claim: Al-Aʿmash transmits from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi a reading with falaq rather than fāliq and a kasra on the hamza.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r17.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي أنه قرأ ( فلق الإصباح )

NAHHAS:v2p82/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r18.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p82/r18.claim: These readers use jaʿala, ‘He made the night a resting place’; Medina reads jāʿil, ‘maker of the night.’
NAHHAS:v2p82/r18.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي ( وجعل الليل سكنا )

NAHHAS:v2p82/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r19.claim: The sun and moon are accusative by coordination with the implied object of jaʿala; genitive coordination is weak because its governor is weak and the elements are separated.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r19.anchor: نصب الشمس والقمر عطفا على المعنى أي وجعل والخفض بعيد

NAHHAS:v2p82/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r20.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب السكوني
NAHHAS:v2p82/r20.claim: Yazid ibn Qutayb al-Sakuni reads the sun and moon in the genitive, coordinated by form with jāʿil.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r20.anchor: وقد قرأ يزيد بن قطيب السكوني ( وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر )

NAHHAS:v2p82/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r21.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p82/r21.claim: Al-Akhfash says ḥusbānan means ‘by calculation’ and is a plural like shihāb and shuhbān.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r21.anchor: وقال الأخفش حسبانا أي بحسبان قال وهو جمع حساب

NAHHAS:v2p82/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r22.speaker: يعقوب
NAHHAS:v2p82/r22.claim: Yaʿqub analyzes ḥusbān as a verbal noun of ḥasiba; ḥisāb is the noun for calculation.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r22.anchor: وقال يعقوب حسبان مصدر حسبت الشيء أحسبه حسبا

NAHHAS:v2p82/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r23.claim: Another explanation is that the sun and moon follow measured courses that neither increase nor diminish, demonstrating God’s power and oneness.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r23.anchor: وقال غيره جعل الله جل وعز سير الشمس والقمر بحساب لا يزيد

NAHHAS:v2p82/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r24.claim: The closing phrase is a subject-predicate sentence.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r24.anchor: ( ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم ) ابتداء وخبر

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.claim: Unlike Al Imran's change-filled context, Al Anam presents God's attributes, power, and favor; its opening nouns and noun forms fit that setting, with a verb for living movement.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f7.anchor: في حين أن السياق في سورة الأنعام مختلف وليس السياق في التغييرات وإنما هو في صفات الله تعالى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r3.claim: With alif and genitive layl, the active participle is coordinated with another participle; the author calls this the better, more common reading and connects it to what already happened.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r3.anchor: فالحجة لمن أثبت الألف وخفض أنه رد لفظ فاعل على مثله وأضاف بمعنى ما قد مضى وثبت

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r4.claim: Without alif and with accusative layl, the phrase is a past verb coordinated by meaning, not form, with the active participle; Arabic poetry offers a parallel.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن حذفها ونصب أنه جعله فعلا ماضيا وعطفه على فاعل معنى لا لفظا كما عطفت العرب اسم الفاعل على الماضي

NASHR:v2p259/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p259/r14.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v2p259/r14.claim: The Kufis read جعل without alif, with a fatḥa on its ʿayn and on al-layl, making night its object.
NASHR:v2p259/r14.anchor: فقرأ الكوفيون وجعل بفتح العين واللام من غير ألف وبنصب اللام من الليل

NASHR:v2p259/r15.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p259/r15.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p259/r15.claim: The other readers use جاعل with alif, kasra on the ʿayn, and the genitive al-layl.
NASHR:v2p259/r15.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالألف وكسر العين ورفع اللام وخفض " الليل "

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.claim: Sībawayh compares this accusative to والشمس والقمر حسبانا: جاعل الليل implies جعل, so the following item is construed on the implied verb.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمررتبهفإذالهصوتصوتحمارو.anchor: فصار كأنه قال وجعل الليل سكنا وحمل

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses splitting the dawn as creating night and day.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فالق الإصباح} قال: خلق الليل والنهار

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the dawn as sunlight by day and moonlight by night.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فالق الإصباح} قال: يعني بالاصباح ضوء الشمس بالنهار

BUKHARI:6982/r8.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BUKHARI:6982/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the cleaver of daybreak as the sun's light by day and the moon's light by night.
BUKHARI:6982/r8.anchor: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ ‏{‏فَالِقُ الإِصْبَاحِ‏}‏ ضَوْءُ الشَّمْسِ بِالنَّهَارِ، وَضَوْءُ الْقَمَرِ بِاللَّيْلِ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p905/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p905/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p905/r2.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ is unqualified and enduring, while making night a repose and sun and moon a reckoning presupposes people who sleep or calculate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p905/r2.anchor: قيّده بمنتفع وهو من يسكن فإن لم يكن هناك من يسكن
